articles.title: Crystal Lake Showrunner on Retelling the Friday the 13th Story: ‘It's Always Ripe for Reinterpretation’
articles.summary: We spoke to Crystal Lake showrunner Brad Caleb Kane, star Linda Cardellini, and other cast members about retelling the Friday the 13th story.
articles.body:
Spoilers follow for the first episode of Crystal Lake , which debuts on Peacock on October 15!

The cast and creator of Crystal Lake showed up at New York Comic Con this week to prep fans for their Friday the 13th sequel series as they prepare for its launch next week. That included a panel discussion, a Camp Crystal Lake activation experience , and a screening of the first episode of the show. I also got a chance to talk to the group about the long-awaited return to the hunting grounds of Jason Voorhees… and his mom Pamela. Don’t forget about Pamela!

We’ll have a full season review of Crystal Lake in a few days, but for now I’m going to break down the biggest points from Episode 1, as well as some thoughts from showrunner Brad Caleb Kane, star Linda Cardellini, and the other cast members who were in attendance. So let’s take a swim in the lake…!

Right out of the gate, the episode gives us Linda Cardellini’s Pamela covered in blood, leaning over a bathroom sink and staring at herself in the mirror. She finds a human tooth embedded in one of her knuckles and says to herself, “What did you do…?”

Of course, we know from 1980’s original Friday the 13th movie that Pam has some slicing and dicing skills. For while her son Jason is the main slasher of the franchise, it was actually Pam who was the killer in that first film, having gone mad after her son drowned (or seemed to drown – more on that in a second) at Camp Crystal.

What becomes clear as the first episode of Crystal Lake proceeds is that while this version of Pam isn’t insane (or perhaps, isn’t insane yet ), she definitely is capable of violence.

“There's a switch,” the actress, who just won an Emmy for the HBO series DTF St. Louis, tells me. “If you flip it with her, there's no going back. It's almost like she doesn't even understand what she's doing. If someone flips that switch, there's a loss of control for her. In a way, she's looking for control and then she loses it at the same time. That's the dangerous dance there.”

“I like to think there's nobody more dangerous than a mother whose child is threatened,” adds Brad Caleb Kane.

“Also, it’s somebody you don't expect,” continues Cardellini. “I think that's part of it that I really enjoyed – is that here's this person who you can kind of relate to, but there's a massive rage underneath there that if you tap into it and start to open that Pandora's box, you can't put that genie back in the bottle.”

Adds the showrunner: “At a certain point, maybe it also feels a little good to let that genie happen.”

Everyone knows Jason Voorhees’ origin story, right? It’s like required reading in schools these days, isn’t it? But what’s interesting about the master of hockey mask couture is that we’ve never really seen much of his childhood, despite his appearing in 12 movies (ish – he’s actually dead in the fifth film) to date, and decades of various ancillary media. Yes, we know he was deformed in some way, and that though believed drowned, the adult Jason took over the teenager-killing duties at Camp Crystal after his mother died in the first film.

But in Crystal Lake, Caleb Kane has decided to give us a young Jason (played by Callum Vinson, who’s also appeared in the Chucky TV series) who is just a cute kid who happens to be a person with some kind of physical disability. And yes, that includes a large, malformed head. I asked the showrunner how he landed on this portrayal of Jason.

“Invention and being really well versed in the movies,” he says. “The end of the first movie, he really is – the way [make-up effects legend Tom] Savini built him, he's sort of monstrous and he's meant just to be this idea that sent Pam on her journey. But if we're doing a show about how Pam lost him, you want to see the connection between mother and child. You want Jason to be a real 11-year-old boy, obviously with differences and difficulties. The iteration of Jason here really came out of the point where we were making a show about a relationship between mother and child. What is that? Who is Jason within the context of that relationship? How does losing him set Pam on this journey? So that's where it came from.”

Cardellini adds that her son is “everything to Pam” but also “he's everything to the franchise.” Indeed, it would’ve been odd to do this show and not include Jason in some way.

“She just loves him more than anything,” says the actress. “Brad wrote this line that they're connected at the heart, and I think that is really at the core of it all – that she never feels disconnected from him. I think the codependency and the inter-connectedness is very, very deep and almost, I don't know, telepathic.”

Since this show is the origin story of Jason as much as it’s Pam’s story, there are certain key moments in the timeline that just have to happen. And certainly one of the most important of those is Jason drowning while the camp counselors aren’t paying attention – as Betsy Palmer’s version of Pam says in the first film, “They were making love while that young boy drowned!” And so it goes in Episode 1 of Crystal Lake that Jason must drown in order for Pam’s journey to really begin.

But Jason can’t really be dead, can he? The question for a show like this is how the writers can build a full season of television without violating the canon that’s already been established… Unless there’s room to change some things, that is.

“I mean, if you watch the [film] series, it changes things from movie to movie,” says Caleb Kane. “I think there's always room and I think it's always ripe for reinterpretation. I think fans of the franchise are going to love certain movies and they don't love certain movies and the fandom is pretty rabid. As a longtime fan, as somebody who knows these movies, their novelizations, all of the things sort of chapter and verse, I felt like I had a little bit of license to play. Also, you’ve got to make sure that you give the fans what they want.”

One area where Caleb Kane and the writers seem to be taking some license is in where Jason and Pam came from before arriving at Crystal Lake. There is a hint of a past involving something called “Argonaut” – we just see a flashback with that name on a door at the end of a long corridor. What does it all mean? We’ll have to wait and see…

The showrunner does offer a hint, however: “What you learn about [Pam] later on in the series is that she did a lot to protect him and get him out of a pretty difficult situation, and herself. When you put that amount of attention on protecting someone and loving someone, their absence is going to be that much more acute.”

Remember what I said about Pam and the tooth embedded in her knuckle? Well, just wait until you see how that tooth winds up where it does. Basically, Crystal Lake gives fans plenty of blood and over-the-top gore… and there’s some sex thrown in there as well.

“The thing has to go full Friday the 13th at a certain point,” says Caleb Kane. “We made sure we did that in the show.”

At the same time, these scenes – at least as far as the pilot episode goes – don’t just feature sex and violence for the sake of it. They help drive the plot and also give us insight into the characters. That said, there’s one scene here that approaches a gross-out level that is just plain funny – in a good way. You gotta see it for yourself, so I won’t even try to explain it.

The Other Residents of Crystal Lake Are Pretty Interesting Too

As a TV series, Crystal Lake needs a supporting cast, and some of the folks we meet are pretty interesting. William Catlett plays Sheriff Levon Brooks, a friend of Pam’s who used to be a cop in the city and seems a bit adrift out in the woods of Crystal Lake. He might also be interested in Pam as perhaps more than a friend, but knowing where she’s heading as we do, that doesn’t seem destined to work out for the sheriff.

“You know, I think you can have two things, two wishes at the same time within your mind,” says Catlett of playing the character, even though he knows where Pam will end up one day. “You love Pam, you want to be with Pam, it's a new beginning, but at the same time it's like, who is this woman? And so if I don't judge it, then I can allow myself to have those emotions that go through with it.”

Gwendolyn Sundstrom plays a character named Grace who is in her early teens and is one of Jason’s only friends. When he seemingly dies, it sends her on a trajectory that could be dangerous for the young girl.

“I think it's losing the most important person in your life,” says Sundstrom. “Losing Jason, to Grace, is something that brings a lot of trauma, and I think that definitely plays into the rest of the season too. It’s something that Grace really struggles with, and she doesn't want it to happen. She definitely wants it to reverse.”

There are also a couple of legacy characters from the first film who pop up as younger versions of themselves, including “Crazy” Ralph (played by Walt Gorney in the original series and Nick Cordileone in Crystal Lake) and Officer Dorf (played by Ron Millkie in the first film and Cameron Scoggins in Crystal Lake). Dorf actually survives the original movie, which means Scoggins has something of an insurance policy here!

“Yeah, he makes it!” laughs Scoggins. “He doesn't die as far as we know in the first movie. We'll see. He appears so briefly in that first movie that you almost do have to go back and watch it sometimes, but it is a memorable little character, and you kind of wonder, where's that guy coming from? And it's just so fun to take such a brief scene and expand upon that and just take the energy of a different actor and be like, well, how are we going to build on this more?”

We’ll see how Crystal Lake builds on the Friday the 13th canon more when it debuts on Peacock on October 15…

articles.title: Image Comics' Roam Reunites Paper Girls Creators Brian K. Vaughan and Cliff Chiang
articles.summary: In one of the coolest announcements to come out of NYCC, IGN can exclusively reveal that Paper Girls creators Brian K. Vaughan and Cliff Chiang are reuniting for a new series called Roam.
articles.body:
In what is easily one of the most exciting comic book-related announcements to come out of NYCC 2026, IGN can exclusively reveal that Paper Girls creators Brian K. Vaughan and Cliff Chiang are reuniting for a new project at Image Comics. That series is called Roam, and it's their first collaboration in over a decade.

The creative team on Roam also includes colorist Matt Wilson and letterer Jared Fletcher. Here's the official description for Roam:

In the future, everyone gets to be a superhero… but only while you’re young.

From the Eisner Award-winning team behind Paper Girls, ROAM reunites Saga writer Brian K. Vaughan and Catwoman: Lonely City creator Cliff Chiang for their first new ONGOING SERIES in over a decade.

Exploring the power and peril that comes with new adulthood, ROAM is a timeless adventure about the quest we each take in life to finally find our team.

The action-packed 50-page (!!!) first issue arrives in comic stores this February 2027!

“Cliff has already drawn the first several issues of ROAM, and I can’t wait for readers to see this breathtakingly original world he and our gifted collaborators Matt and Jared helped create," Vaughan tells IGN. "Thanks so much to the readers and retailers out here who are up for exploring something new with us!"

"There's no bigger thrill than breathing life into new worlds with your friends, that electric feeling of collaboration," Chiang says. "ROAM is unlike anything Brian and I have done before, but inspired by our love for comics as a medium. It's been a joy to reunite with our trusted teammates Matt Wilson and Jared Fletcher, and I'm incredibly grateful to Image Comics for continuing the creative partnership and exploration that began with Paper Girls. It's going to be a wild ride!"

Roam #1 will be released in February 2027, and it's already shaping up to be one of our most anticipated new comics of the eyar. You can preorder a copy at your local comic shop .

articles.title: Arc Raiders' 2.0 Update and 'Spider-Man' Grappling Hook Drive Player Count to Reach 7-Month High
articles.summary: The new Arc Raiders 2.0 update has triggered a seven-month high for its concurrent player count on Steam as fans show up for its "Spider-Man" grappling hook, a new map, a free weekend, and more.
articles.body:
The new Arc Raiders 2.0 update has triggered a seven-month high for its concurrent player count on Steam as fans show up for its "Spider-Man" grappling hook, a new map, a free weekend, and more.

Embark's once-viral extraction experience has had a rough few months. As the studio slowed down updates and vowed to rework its divisive Expedition prestige system , Arc Raiders players have largely left it behind, hoping to one day return to Speranza should more enticing updates arrive.

After reaching an all-time peak of nearly 500,000 players on Steam (via SteamDB ), it's consistently struggled to reach more than 35,000 players on PC since July. It was a fall from grace that's left fans missing the honeymoon phase, but the Frozen Trail update, which launched two days ago, October 8, across PC, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X/S, has almost immediately brought back some of that hype.

In September, Arc Raiders reached a player count low of just 10,000 on Steam. As of the publication of this story, 166,670 people are logged onto Arc Raiders on the PC platform alone, and it looks like it could keep climbing. It's a number Embark hasn't hit since early April, and although it's too soon to tell if these are the kind of results needed to give it a proper second wind, it does mark the first time the game has achieved a notable spike since December 2025.

It's all thanks to Frozen Trail and the free weekend that helped usher it in. The update, which brought the first substantial changes Arc Raiders has received since Riven Tides in April , introduced a collection of game-changing content. Its crown jewel is Pendola Pass, a snowy mountainous region located beyond Raiders' usual home in the Rust Belt. New buildings to loot and shoot through would surely be enough to bring fans back, but it's really just the tip of the iceberg.

New Arc threats like the Bully, Skulker, and Hydra have shaken up combat encounters. The Tether Launcher, which can tie enemies to objects against their will, and the Grappling Hook have given players new tools to experiment with. That aforementioned free weekend, meanwhile, which runs from October 8 – 12, has allowed even newcomers to check out how Embark has changed Arc Raiders for the better. Individually, these are updates that would pique the interest of even the most casual fan, but the only reason so many are installing the game again is because of how these tweaks add new toys to the sandbox.

"I was not a believer," one popular post on Reddit said . "This is one of the best updates ever in a video game."

The same post continued, first praising Frozen Trail's scale. They admitted to being a lapsed Arc Raiders fan, explaining that the mix of Embark's new elements not only got them to return but also has them looking forward to what's next.

"I absolutely loved Arc Raiders for its first 6 months but I got frustrated with it since they announced the twice a year update," they said. "I quit playing, said that these devs don’t know what they’re doing, they fumbled, etc. I know it probably won’t reach the popularity and number of players it had in December but that doesn’t matter to me, what matters to me is that I was flat out wrong about these devs and their ability to update the game. What they did here is special and I just wanted to come out and admit I was wrong and give them their flowers. I’m now extremely excited for the future of this game."

While not everyone is willing to go as far as to call it an all-time great video game update, it's hard to find anyone being too critical of what Embark had to offer. Pendola Pass' size seems to be an especially notable bright spot, with others mentioning the new UFO-style Arc ship known as the Frigate as another big highlight.

"I agree, not to mention the new weapons, skills, weapons mods, it’s hard to believe they did all this in less than 6 months. Frigate is so damn cool," another said .

With such a drastic and sudden increase in attention, more highlight reels have started to find their way back to social media, too. New tools like the Grappling Hook come with obvious opportunities for shareable clips, as it allows Raiders to attach to everything from steep cliffs to flying Arc. Others can't help but draw comparisons to how the toy allows players to swing through maps like "Spider-Man."

"I was going to get that," one fan said , referring to a new wall-running skill, "but then I remembered grappling hooks exist now. It's sooo much more fun to swing around like Spider-Man and then run around at 100mph with no stamina usage."

There's also the new Advanced Camera. It works exactly how you'd expect, giving players the tech to capture memories, all with the click of a button. Considering Arc Raiders has thrived on the comedy presented by its in-game systems, a camera has really only given that chaos another chance to shine.

Arc Raiders is having a bit of a moment, but we'll have to see if it has truly managed to recapture the magic that made it such a hit at launch. Up next is testing for a dedicated PvE mode , something fans have begged to see implemented since launch. Embark is certainly at least trying, with the game also available for 50% off on all platforms as players flock to its free weekend.

IGN gave Arc Raiders a 9/10 review when it arrived almost exactly one year ago, saying, "With polished gunplay and an irresistible grind, Arc Raiders sets a new standard for extraction shooters." Even if Embark can't entertain a consistently high number of players, it's clear the studio has more plans for the IP in the future. Both it and the studio's game-show-inspired FPS, The Finals, are set to receive TV show and movie adaptations at some point in the future .

Frozen Trail brought more new content to Arc Raiders than we could list. You can see the full patch notes below.

Arc Raiders Frozen Trail Update 2.0 Patch Notes

The cold has arrived, and it's brought a lot with it. Frozen Trail is our biggest update since launch, packed with new features, fresh challenges, and a long list of fixes and improvements.

We've been working on this one for a while, and we couldn't be more excited to finally put it in your hands. Whether you're here for the new content or just want to know what we've fixed, there's something for everyone. Grab something warm, settle in, and read on for the full breakdown.

Thank you for playing, for reporting bugs, and for sticking with us.

Changes to the Raider Skill Tree include new skills and improvements to existing skills, enabling players to better embellish their playstyle with more impactful skill choices.

We've heard the comments (and seen in the data) that the Skill Tree was not living up to its role in offering sufficiently interesting ways of building your character to better define and refine your playstyle. The goal of the Skill Tree revamp is twofold: to look at under-performing skills, modify or replace them, and to get closer to the goal of making choice and expression a more core feature of the Skill Tree.

Alongside some new skills and a reshuffling of the layout, new functionality has been added to replace the previous 'large' nodes at the middle and end of the branches. Now, for the middle of each branch, instead of having two selectable skills and two 'paths', there is one path where the node is a binary choice between two skills. You can only choose one; you will be able to make the choice again when you reset your skill tree. At the end of each branch are two nodes where you must make a choice out of three skills. Here, you can choose up to two of the three, after reaching the required skill point investment.

As this is a fairly big reimagining of the Skill Tree, there will likely be more tweaks and updates in the near future, to existing and new skills, as we see how you are engaging with it.

articles.title: Christian Yelich isn’t letting ‘commentary’ dictate Brewers’ mindset vs. Dodgers
articles.summary: The Milwaukee Brewers and the Los Angeles Dodgers are preparing to square off in the National League Championship Series. The series gets underway Sunday in...
articles.body:
The Milwaukee Brewers and the Los Angeles Dodgers are preparing to square off in the National League Championship Series. The series gets underway Sunday in Milwaukee, and the Brewers will have homefield advantage.

Milwaukee had the best record in the National League with a 103-59 record. However, the Dodgers have won back-to-back World Series titles and they are attempting to become the first National League team to win three consecutive Fall Classics.

Before the Dodgers can square off with the American League champions, they have to win this series. Jacob Misiorowski will take the mound for the Brewers in Game 1, while two-time Cy Young Award winner Tarik Skubal will get the start for the Dodgers.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

The oddsmakers have made Misiorowski and the Brewers slight favorites (-113) to win Game 1 of the series. However, veteran Brewer Christian Yelich is not concerned with any discussion of which team is favored or which team is the underdog in the series.

"It doesn't matter what the commentary is surrounding the series, who's the favorite, who's the underdog," Yelich said , per Brewers beat writer Adam McCalvy. "It's going to be decided on the field."

The Brewers defeated the San Diego Padres in the National League Division Series to earn their spot in the NLCS. After winning the first two games at home, the Brewers lost Game 3 in San Diego before winning the fourth game on the road.

The Dodgers defeated the Atlanta Braves in four games to get back to the NLCS. After splitting the first two games at Dodger Stadium, the Dodgers clinched the series by winning consecutive games in Atlanta.

articles.title: ALDS Game 5 – White Sox at Guardians discussion
articles.summary: Which AL Central team will head to sunny Florida this weekend?
articles.body:
The White Sox and Guardians are the only teams to take their ALDS all the way to the limit. It's been a battle of bad offenses to this point, with the Guardians exploding all over White Sox postseason hero Grant Taylor in Game 4 to force the winner-take-all finale.

Gavin Williams, the veteran ace of the Guardians, will take the ball in the top of the first inning. The White Sox, who have mostly leaned on their bullpen through the first six games of their 2026 playoff experience, will turn to the closest thing they have to their own ace in Sean Burke to start things off. This is a series finale, though, so expect all hands on deck and to potentially even see guys who pitched a lot on Thursday night like Parker Messick and Erick Fedde take the ball.

I can't promise the baseball will be good, but it should at least be fun!

articles.title: ALDS Game 5 open chat
articles.summary: After taking a 2-0 lead, the White Sox will try not to blow the series on the road.
articles.body:
Poor Chicago. That could have gone better. After going up 2-0 against Cleveland in the American League Division Series, the White Sox returned home with a chance to clinch a playoff series at home for the first time since 1906. They failed to do that, though, dropping Games 3 and 4, in which Cleveland's offense erupted for nine runs each night.

Is Chicago's pitching simply exhausted? It looks like it. On Thursday night, Chicago used seven pitchers in the loss, including closer Grant Taylor, who got hit hard in a six-run sixth inning for Cleveland. The White Sox staff is also a little wild: they walked 10 batters in Wednesday's 9-3 loss and seven more with a hit batter on Thursday.

On the other hand, Cleveland had to use their ace starting pitcher Gavin Williams to get the last three outs in Game 4. Williams started the Guardians' 4-3 loss in Game 2 on Monday, and was scheduled to pitch Game 5 on normal rest. But he's out on the mound again, giving his team a spot start in a win-or-go-home situation.

With everything on the line, Chicago is handing the game ball to right-hander Sean Burke, who'll start on the road tonight at Progressive Field. Burke was efficient in Game 2, entering in the third and striking out six Guardians over 5 1/3 innings while allowing one run on one hit. This time, Chicago isn't pairing him with an opener.

Both teams are grateful for yesterday's day off. So who do you think will win Game 5 of the ALDS to face the Rays next week?

articles.body:
Prime Video has published a new Blade Runner 2099 trailer, revealing more about the mystery surrounding its missing Replicants, as well as the roles Hunter Schafer and Michelle Yeoh play in the story.

This more detailed look at the Amazon-backed limited series and its dystopian sci-fi setting arrived at New York Comic Con 2026. Attendees at the Blade Runner 2099 panel were treated to the new trailer in person, with both it and a new poster now available for all to see online.

Starring Schafer (Euphoria) and Yeoh (Everything Everywhere All at Once) as Cora and Olwen, respectively, Blade Runner 2099 is set to premiere in November. You can see the NYCC 2026 trailer below.

A new world. A new order. A new Blade Runner. Blade Runner 2099, a new limited series, premieres November 25th on Prime Video. — prime video IN (@PrimeVideoIN) October 10, 2026

A new world. A new order. A new Blade Runner. Blade Runner 2099, a new limited series, premieres November 25th on Prime Video.

"Fifty years after the events of Blade Runner 2049, Los Angeles has been reborn, just not by humanity," an official description from Prime Video said. "Cora, a fugitive in a final bid to stop running, takes on one last identity: a Blade Runner. Forced to partner with Olwen, a Replicant days from dying, she hunts down a runaway hiding a truth that could collapse a fragile city."

Today's comic-con trailer fills in some of the blanks left by the teaser revealed at San Diego Comic-Con this past July. Set 50 years after Ryan Gosling's Blade Runner 2049 and 80 years after Harrison Ford's original movie, Yeoh's Olwen can be heard saying 10 female and 18 male Replicants have gone missing in the last year. Amid tense words from Schafer's character, viewers are told that a mysterious "he" is out there, and he "knows the cure for all Replicants."

"I don't know what you're doing," Yeoh's Olwen says as the trailer closes. "Do you?"

The Blade Runner 2099 NYCC 2026 trailer provided a closer look into a mystery that certainly looks like it will fit in with past entries, but we'll have to wait until its November 25, 2026, release date to see how all of the pieces will come together. Its binge release plan will see all eight episodes available to stream on the same day.

With both Ridley Scott's '80s original film and Denis Villeneuve's legacy sequel enjoying a dedicated following to this day, there's already a lot of hype behind Blade Runner 2099. For more while we wait, you can read IGN's new NYCC interview with showrunner Silka Luisa .

articles.title: Naruto Teasers Reveal New Shadow Rising Manga and Anime Crossover Series
articles.summary: Naruto is alive and well, as author Masashi Kishimoto has announced a new manga called Shadow Rising – and a new anime crossover series is on the way, too.
articles.body:
Naruto is alive and well, as author Masashi Kishimoto has announced a new manga called Shadow Rising – and a new anime crossover series is on the way, too.

Both Naruto projects were announced during the Naruto panel at New York Comic Con 2026. Details about the manga, specifically, were light, with only Kishimoto's involvement and its "Shadow Rising" title confirmed for now.

The panel did come with more information about that anime series, though. Aptly titled "Naruto x Ninku," the show will serve as a full-on crossover between Naruto and popular '90s manga and anime franchise Ninku . Both the show and the manga did receive teaser trailers, which you can see below.

A teaser for new NARUTO manga by Masashi Kishimoto is here! Stay tuned for more updates at the NARUTO Super Stage at Jump Festa 2027! #PROJECT_RASENGAN #NARUTO #JumpFesta — NARUTO OFFICIAL (@NARUTO_info_en) October 10, 2026

A teaser for new NARUTO manga by Masashi Kishimoto is here! Stay tuned for more updates at the NARUTO Super Stage at Jump Festa 2027! #PROJECT_RASENGAN #NARUTO #JumpFesta

Two legendary shinobi series collide. Fully supervised by Koji Kiriyama and Masashi Kishimoto, NARUTO x NINKŪ is in production! Director: Noriyuki Abe Character Designer / Chief Animation Director: Tetsuya Nishio #PROJECT_RASENGAN #NARUTO #NINKU — NARUTO OFFICIAL (@NARUTO_info_en) October 10, 2026

Two legendary shinobi series collide. Fully supervised by Koji Kiriyama and Masashi Kishimoto, NARUTO x NINKŪ is in production! Director: Noriyuki Abe Character Designer / Chief Animation Director: Tetsuya Nishio #PROJECT_RASENGAN #NARUTO #NINKU

"Team 7 members Naruto, Sasuke, and Sakura are given a mission by Kakashi," an official description for Naruto x Ninku said. "Since Kakashi cannot participate himself, Naruto is appointed acting leader. As a result of this decision, Naruto is fully motivated to make the mission a success. However, on the way, Team 7 finds themselves lost in another world. What appears before the bewildered trio is a boy with a face resembling a frog’s, named Fūsuke. What awaits them in this strange new world?"

Meanwhile, as reported by Variety , the Naruto panel also came with a surprise update on the live-action movie . Amid rumors of early plot details and casting decisions, director Destin Daniel Cretton shared a message where he explained "what an honor it is to bring Kishimoto-sensei's incredible world and characters to life."

"The further we get into making this film, the more excited I am about what we’re creating," he continued. "What I’ve always loved about Naruto is that he’s the character who might normally get sidelined as a sidekick. He’s excitable, he tries too hard, and people underestimate him. But he has an incredible heart. No matter how many times he fails or gets knocked down, he never stops believing in himself or fighting for the people he loves. That spirit is at the heart of the story we’re telling.

"These characters mean so much to so many people, myself included, and I carry that with me as we make this film. We’re approaching the world, relationships, and journeys Kishimoto-sensei created with a lot of care, and we want to capture what makes NARUTO so special. We’re hard at work and will have more to share soon. Until then, thank you for your passion, your patience, and for being along for the ride. I can’t wait for you to see what’s ahead!"

A description in the YouTube upload for Shadow Rising promised more details will be shared at the Naruto Super Stage at Jump Festa 2027. The Naruto x Ninku upload , meanwhile, confirmed that the show is in production with supervision from Kishimoto and Ninku author Koji Kiriyama, with the Naruto X/Twitter account confirming Noriyuki Abe as its director and Tetsuya Nishio as its character designer/chief animation director. Release date details remain a mystery for now.

articles.title: Dodgers’ Tarik Skubal is embracing the pressure of pitching Game 1 vs. Brewers for LA
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Dodgers are four wins away from another World Series trip, and they are handing the ball to Tarik Skubal to start the process. The two-time...
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are four wins away from another World Series trip, and they are handing the ball to Tarik Skubal to start the process. The two-time Cy Young Award winner will face the Milwaukee Brewers in Game 1 of the National League Championship Series on Sunday, and he is embracing everything that comes with it.

Asked about the pressure surrounding Los Angeles as it chases a third straight championship, Skubal welcomed it .

"The pressure surrounding the Dodgers is a privilege," Skubal said. "As an athlete, this is what you want to be, and you want to have an expectation to win. I have those same expectations as a player, and in my shoes, I think just keeping the game the game, going out there and competing and doing what I can to put my team in a position to win is important."

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

That mindset has already served him well this October. Skubal started Game 1 of the NL Division Series against the Atlanta Braves and allowed just one run on two hits over six innings, striking out seven in a 5-3 win.

Los Angeles went on to eliminate Atlanta in four games, while Milwaukee knocked out the San Diego Padres in four to set up a rematch of last year's NLCS.

Skubal will be opposed by Brewers ace Jacob Misiorowski , who has given the Dodgers fits. In two regular-season starts and one relief appearance in last year's NLCS, the right-hander has posted a 1.59 ERA with 27 strikeouts and only three walks across 17 innings against Los Angeles.

Game 1 will be played at American Family Field, where Milwaukee will also host Game 2 on Monday. Yoshinobu Yamamoto is lined up to start that game for the Dodgers, giving manager Dave Roberts two aces at the front of his rotation.

The Dodgers may also have a roster decision to make. Infielder Miguel Rojas left Game 3 against Atlanta with lower back pain , and Roberts said there was "nothing definitive" on his status heading into the series.

For Skubal, the assignment is exactly what the Dodgers envisioned when they brought him to Los Angeles. If his words are any indication, he is ready for the moment.

articles.title: Guardians make playoff strikeout history in ALDS win over White Sox
articles.summary: The Cleveland Guardians needed every bit of their pitching staff to climb out of a 0-2 hole against the Chicago White Sox. By the time they finished, they ha...
articles.body:
The Cleveland Guardians needed every bit of their pitching staff to climb out of a 0-2 hole against the Chicago White Sox. By the time they finished, they had rewritten the postseason record book. Cleveland beat Chicago 2-0 in a rainy Game 5 of the American League Division Series on Saturday at Progressive Field, completing a comeback from two games down.

Along the way, Guardians pitchers struck out 75 White Sox hitters, the most ever in a postseason series lasting five games.

According to Talkin' Baseball , only three postseason series in MLB history have produced more strikeouts, and all of them went the full seven games. CBS Sports noted that the total also shattered the previous Division Series record of 64.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

The final night was a fitting exclamation point. Chicago struck out 21 times in Game 5, with starter Gavin Williams doing much of the damage. The right-hander allowed just one hit over 5 2/3 scoreless innings, walking two and striking out 12 to tie Charles Nagy's franchise record for strikeouts in a postseason game.

Jose Ramirez provided all the offense Cleveland needed with a two-run homer in the fourth inning. The veteran turned on a two-strike curveball for the lowest pitch he has ever homered on in his career.

The strikeout parade had been building all series. In Game 3, the White Sox went down on strikes 19 times as Cleveland won 9-3 at Rate Field to stay alive. Reliever Foster Griffin set a franchise postseason record for a reliever with seven strikeouts in that game.

The Guardians then forced a decisive fifth game with a 9-5 win in Game 4 , erupting for six runs in the sixth inning. Travis Bazzana delivered the go-ahead double, and Patrick Bailey and Ramírez both homered.

Chicago, which swept the Houston Astros in the Wild Card Series for its first playoff series win since 2005, saw its surprising run end one win short of the ALCS.

Cleveland became just the seventh team in the Wild Card era to come back from an 0-2 deficit in a best-of-five series. The Guardians now advance to face the Tampa Bay Rays in the AL Championship Series, with Game 1 set for Monday at Tropicana Field.

articles.title: Column: After a painful knockout blow in the ALDS, the Chicago White Sox vow to get back up
articles.summary: CLEVELAND — Three years after knocking out Tim Anderson, Cleveland Guardians third baseman José Ramírez knocked the Chicago White Sox out of the postseason....
articles.body:
CLEVELAND — Three years after knocking out Tim Anderson, Cleveland Guardians third baseman José Ramírez knocked the Chicago White Sox out of the postseason.

Or did the White Sox knock themselves out?

It was hard to tell after the Guardians beat the Sox 2-0 in Game 5 of the American League Division Series on Saturday at Progressive Field, taking the final three games after putting themselves in an 0-2 hole.

Ramírez's two-run fourth-inning home run off Sean Burke gave the Guardians the lead, and the Sox were already down for the count. They didn't notch a hit off starter Gavin Williams until two outs in the sixth, and struck out a major-league record 21 times —including 12 by Williams — in a listless offensive performance that sent them home.

So a storybook Sox season turned into a fractured fairy tale in the end. For 6 1/2 months it was a moon-age dream. And for the last three games it was a Freddy Krueger-like nightmare.

"Not running out of gas," left fielder Sam Antonacci said. "Just a little uptick with the chase rate, and they threw some really good arms. But credit to their arms and a lack of awareness of the zone on our end."

The Guardians had 52 combined strikeouts in the Sox's three losses — a postseason record 19 in Game 3, 12 in Game 4 and then breaking the Game 3 record on Saturday with 21. Their 75 strikeouts in five games also set an ALDS record.

"They pitched their asses off those last three games," Antonacci said. "And it felt like we were allergic to that big hit."

Williams struck out 12 of the 21 hitters he faced, tying a Guardians' postseason record, and threw 5 2/3 hitless innings until Kyle Teel singled in the sixth. The Sox finished with three hits and wound up batting .211 in the postseason with four home runs, 11 extra-base hits and 96 strikeouts in seven games.

The only real scoring opportunity for the Sox on Saturday came in the sixth after Williams walked Miguel Vargas to load the bases. Left-hander Erik Sabrowski came on to strike out Munetaka Murakami and end the threat. Venable said he did not consider using Randal Grichuk to pinch-hit in that situation. Murakami struck out four times and hit .179 with 16 strikeouts in 27 at-bats in the seven postseason games.

Asked what he needs to do to get to another level, Murakami was honest about his deficiencies.

"My first priority is to prevent injuries, not to get injured again," he said through his interpreter. "In the offseason I'll do whatever it takes to put that work in to get stronger and stronger. As for mechanics, I'm still swinging at the high velocity and up pitches, and the breaking balls down. The chase is there. I have to get better in all the mechanics and all the aspects of baseball, and that's what I want to try to improve in the offseason and come back next year."

Murakami helped make the Sox believe in themselves, but his second-half and postseason struggles were too glaring to overlook.

"I think people will remember the season as a whole," outfielder Tristan Peters said. "Obviously it's a bit of a bitter ending, but at the beginning of the year nobody really believed in us, except for us. The fact we got this far surprised a lot of people."

But the fact the Sox had the Guardians down and couldn't knock them out was a bitter pill to swallow, and something that will linger with Sox fans.

"No one was thinking, 'We're up 2-0, it's over,'" second baseman Chase Meidroth said. "You know you're in a fight, and they executed a little better than we did."

Will the ending change how the season is viewed?

"It's hard to look at it and really see what we accomplished this year," Antonacci said. "It will take some time to sit down and look at it. But obviously the goal is the World Series. If anyone says their goal is to make it to the playoffs, it's a piss-poor goal. You play this game to win, and we didn't win. I'm happy, though, because not a lot of baseball players can say they played in the postseason, so that's something to be proud of.

"Obviously it hurts. It's hard to put into words, but me being a rookie, this will be a hard year to surpass, just vibes and emotions and feelings-wise. The characters that this team had will be like no other. The hard part about this business is that this will be the last time this tight-knit group will be together. I'm already looking forward to next year."

Reliever Grant Taylor, a postseason savior for all but Game 4, said the lessons he learned were of a personal nature, including how to support his fiancée better and build better relationships in the clubhouse. Taylor, Burke and Meidroth stood out in the postseason as future stars and leaders in the clubhouse.

"It was a good year on the field," Taylor said. "But it ended a little too soon."

The offensive meltdown was reminiscent of the 1983 "Winning Ugly" White Sox team that hit .211 with no home runs and 2 RBI in a four-game loss to the Baltimore Orioles in the American League Championship Series. Stars Carlton Fisk, Harold Baines, Greg Luzinski and Ron Kittle all disappeared at the plate, ending another dream season.

This team wasn't nearly as talented as the '83 Sox, and didn't have as much overall power as that team. But Murakami, Vargas and Colson Montgomery all hit 30-plus home runs in the regular season, then combined for three home runs in the postseason with 33 strikeouts.

It goes without saying that no one expected the Sox to get this far in the first place. They deserve all the praise in the world for doing that. But few expected them to flop so badly after sweeping Houston, winning the first two games in Cleveland and coming home to a frenzied environment at Rate Field. After being lauded by fans and the media for weeks, they now need to accept the criticism that comes with a collapse .

DH Andrew Benintendi said the ending will take some time to process, but the young team should be proud of its accomplishments.

"It was a hell of a year, and we've got some experience in here now and it will only benefit us later," he said.

It's easy to say this will be the start of better days, but rebuilds aren't always linear. The '83 Sox turned into the '84 Sox, a 74-win team that ceded the city back to the crosstown Cubs. The magic was gone, and by the summer of '86 they fired manager Tony La Russa in a move Chairman Jerry Reinsdorf spent the next 34 years regretting, leading him to rehire La Russa before the 2021 season.

After one postseason win in '21, it was all downhill from there.

The 2026 Sox helped erase the stench of the '22 and '23 seasons, and the record-setting 121-loss season under Pedro Grifol in '24. Venable created a culture that changed perceptions on the South Side, and the young nucleus made believers out of skeptics.

With a lockout looming, no one knows what 2027 holds for MLB. It could be a while before we see the Sox on the field again. After all the postgame hugs and handshakes, one thing was obvious.

"We've got to be better," Meidroth said. "It's flat-out simple. Be better. All you can do in the offseason, clean up some little things for each person and continue to grow as an individual."

articles.title: Dodgers’ Dave Roberts sends message to Shohei Ohtani before NLCS amid slump
articles.summary: Shohei Ohtani has not looked like himself this October, and the Los Angeles Dodgers are not asking him to carry the load right away. Ahead of Game 1 of the N...
articles.body:
Shohei Ohtani has not looked like himself this October, and the Los Angeles Dodgers are not asking him to carry the load right away. Ahead of Game 1 of the National League Championship Series against the Milwaukee Brewers , manager Dave Roberts lowered the bar for his superstar.

"For tomorrow it's just get on base, take good at-bats, and we'll deal with whatever," Roberts said. "Honestly, it's the same message for everyone. Shohei is known for his slug, but when you're facing Jacob (Misiorowski), it's just you've got to take good at-bats."

Roberts made it clear that any positive contribution will do.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"If you run into a homer, great. But if you can earn a walk, fantastic," Roberts said. "Production is just doing anything positive for the club, and we need all guys to do their part."

Ohtani went just 2-for-13 with four strikeouts and two walks in the NL Division Series against the Atlanta Braves. Roberts even dropped him to fifth in the batting order for Game 3 against left-hander Chris Sale, a move he said was specific to that matchup.

"He's scuffling right now, but I really believe that he's going to come to life at some point," Roberts said during that series.

The slump comes after Ohtani missed most of September with various injuries , giving him only five tune-up games in the final week of the regular season before the playoffs began.

The Dodgers survived anyway. They eliminated Atlanta with a 4-1 win in Game 4 on Wednesday, even as Ohtani, Mookie Betts, Freddie Freeman and Will Smith combined to go 0-for-15 in the clincher.

Misiorowski has been one of the toughest pitchers the Dodgers have faced , posting a 1.59 ERA with 27 strikeouts and just three walks over 17 innings against them in two regular-season starts and one relief appearance in last year's NLCS.

L os Angeles will counter with Tarik Skubal on the mound in Milwaukee, with Yoshinobu Yamamoto lined up for Game 2 on Monday.

Roberts' approach takes some pressure off his star. If Ohtani can simply grind out at-bats against one of the league's most overpowering arms, the Dodgers will gladly take it as they chase a third straight World Series title.

articles.title: Ni Doncic ni Jokic, así serían los premios de la nueva temporada de la NBA según 2K27
articles.standfirst: Hemos ido al videojuego para predecir MVP, Rookie del Año y todos los premios de la NBA
articles.summary: Hemos ido al videojuego para predecir MVP, Rookie del Año y todos los premios de la NBA
articles.body: En menos de 10 días los amantes del baloncesto sonreirán de nuevo ya que empieza una nueva temporada de la NBA, aunque, eso sí, ya nos estamos viniendo arriba con la pretemporada, por ejemplo, viendo el inicio de Aday Mara con la camiseta de los Thunder. Pero una conversación que se tiene siempre a estas alturas tiene que ver precisamente con el futuro, con los premios individuales de final de campaña. Y es que a todos nos gusta hacer predicciones de quién será el MVP, el Rookie del Año…Pero en esta ocasión no seremos nosotros los que nos mojaremos, va a ser NBA 2K27. Decimos esto porque el videojuego será en esta ocasión el encargado de predecir el futuro y para eso nos hemos ido a las estadísticas del 2K para sacar ciertas conclusiones, las que, aunque no sean del todo fiables, nos han dejado claras varias cosas. Por ejemplo en el MVP claro precisamente no ha estado. Para este premio nos hemos ido a la estadística más sencilla de comparar, la valoración general de cada jugador, y aquí nos hemos encontrado un empate entre las tres ‘bestias’ de la NBA. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, Victor Wembanyama y Nikola Jokic tienen la misma valoración, 97, así que había que desempatar de alguna manera. Por eso mismo nos hemos ido a los puntos totales de atributos del jugador, es decir, la suma total de las estadísticas de cada uno de ellos. Y bajo estos números NBA 2K27 habría ‘coronado’ a un jugador con su primer MVP, Victor Wembanyama, el que finalmente adelantaría al canadiense y al serbio para confirmar su gran irrupción del año pasado. Así que mucho ojo con la temporada de los tres a ver si 2K27 lo va a clavar. Y al igual que ocurría en el caso del MVP, cuando hemos querido decidir quién será el Rookie del Año en la NBA nos hemos encontrado con el mismo problema, ya que los tres grandes aspirantes se encontraban igualados con una media de 79. Hablamos de AJ Dybantsa de Washington Wizards, Darryn Peterson de Utah Jazz y Cameron Boozer de Memphis Grizzlies, así que, de nuevo, nos tenemos que ir a los puntos totales de atributos. En esta ocasión NBA 2K27, por muy poca diferencia, ha decidido que el novato de esta temporada en la NBA va a ser Cameron Boozer, una opción que quizá nos sorprende, ya que los otros dos parten con ventaja por su estilo de juego, o eso parece, pero que podría respaldar el hecho de que va a ser el que más libertad va a tener en su equipo para jugarse tiros y desarrollar su propio baloncesto. Vamos ahora con el premio a defensor del año, y a diferencia de los anteriores, NBA 2K27 ha decidido de manera clara y manifiesta, ya que el ganador de este premio sería claramente Victor Wembanyama, el que según 2K27 se llevaría un doblete a final de temporada. Y es que el francés, aunque hay muchos parámetros que engloban la defensa en el videojuego, es el claro líder en consistencia defensiva, IQ defensivo, defensa interior y tapones. Esto no sorprende a nadie, ya que desde hacía muchos años, quizá desde Dwight Howard, no veíamos un dominio defensivo tan grande como el que está imponiendo el francés desde su llegada a la liga. ‘Wemby’ ya se llevó el año pasado este premio y da la sensación de que lo va a ganar todas las temporadas en las que no tenga problemas de lesiones y NBA 2K27 lo sabe y lo ha dejado claro en sus estadísticas. El siguiente premio ya es algo más complicado que los anteriores en los que solo con ver los atributos del juego os servía para sacar conclusiones. Hablamos del Sexto Hombre del Año, y es que claro, en el 2K27 no existe ningún parámetro que mida esto. Por eso mismo nos hemos ido a consultar diferentes webs especializadas sobre la NBA para sacar una lista de los que, a priori, parten como suplentes de cara a esta temporada. Una vez teníamos esto ya era sencillo, ver de todos estos jugadores el que más media tenía. Y así, nos ha salido un nombre claro, Dylan Harper con una valoración de 85, el que por tener a Fox y Castle por delante parte desde el banquillo, aunque en casi cualquier otro equipo de la liga sería titular indiscutible. Esto tendría bastante sentido, pues Harper es un jugador muy especial, con muchos puntos en las manos y en un equipo ganador, así que ojo que NBA 2K27 podría haber acertado de lleno. Y terminamos con el premio más sorprendente, y quizá polémico de todos, el del Jugador Más Mejorado. Para sacar un nombre no lo hemos tenido fácil, ya que aunque haya en el juego un atributo de potencial, cómo lo relacionas con este premio. Pues bien, lo que hemos hecho ha sido fijarnos en este atributo y hemos visto que había un total de 17 jugadores con un potencial A+, el más alto de todos y a partir de ahí hemos trabajado. Una vez teniendo esta lista de 17 hemos ido a ver el jugador que tuviera menos media de todos, es decir, el que menos valoración tenga entre la ‘élite del potencial’. Esto significaría que sería el que más margen de mejora tiene entre su media y a la que podría llegar en su mejor escenario. Y este jugador ha sido nada más y nada menos que Ja Morant con 84 de valoración. Y es que puede parecer una locura porque sería raro darle este premio a un jugador que ya ha sido All-Star, pero tras unos años entre polémicas, lesiones y un rendimiento tan bajo, si Ja Morant es capaz de volver a su mejor versión tras su traspaso a Blazers y ser el mejor jugador de un equipo que gane bastantes más partidos de los que pierde se podría abrir un debate muy interesante. Y así quedan las predicciones de NBA 2K27 sobre los premios de la temporada de la temporada 26/27 de la NBA y lo tienen todo, premios claros, algunos muy ajustados y una ‘bomba’ para despedir. Repetimos, esto es jugar a la ciencia ficción, pero hay veces que la realidad supera a la ficción, por eso habrá que tener mucho ojo con lo que pase este año en la liga de baloncesto más grande del planeta.

articles.title: 23 days till Iowa Hoops: Isaia Howard
articles.summary: Isaiah Howard was a key figure off the bench for last year’s team & will need to continue thriving in his role
articles.body:
While football season is in full swing, it doesn't mean we can't dabble in some basketball prep ahead of the first tip-off on November 3rd! Next up is a UFC fighter masquerading as a basketball player: Isaia Howard!

#23 – Isaia Howard, G, 6'5" 216 lbs 3rd year; Plattsburg, MO; Plattsburg

2025-26 : 37 games, 5.1 PPG, 2.6 RPG, 1.1 APG, 45.0% FG, 28.1% 3P, 69.4% FT, 18.2 MPG

Howard is another former Bulldog who came over with Ben McCollum after Iowa hired him. He had modest stats his freshman season but was an absolute bucket as a high schooler where he finished with 34.4 PPG & 13.2 RPG for Plattsburg. He had 2 games over 50 points his senior season. Dude can fill it up.

He likes to yam; he likes to block; he looks like an absolute menace to go against – just constantly stunting on fools and getting revved up.

That hasn't changed since he's donned the black & gold.

He always plays with energy. Constantly in his opponent's grill on defense. Despite playing just 18 minutes a game he was second on the team in steals with 1 a game.

However some of that scoring has not yet translated to Big Ten basketball consistently. He had just four games in double digits last season, the final one coming on January 6th. Yet his season high of 19 was absolutely integral in getting the Hawks over Grand Canyon in their Thanksgiving tournament. He went 7/10 in 29 minutes. He added six boards, a steal, and a block.

The Plattsburg native will have to develop some offensive consistency this season as the team has added wing depth in high school recruiting. Since the Hawks lost their three top scorers, there is that void in scoring. If he can be a consistent scorer – especially if his 3 point shot can approach 40% – off the bench, it will be a boost to the much needed offense.

It'll make it hard to take him off because it's such a joy to watch him play basketball like a psychopath.

articles.title: MLB Playoff Roundup: Guardians complete comeback, advance to ALCS against Rays
articles.summary: Cleveland will try to upset Tampa Bay for the AL pennant.
articles.body:
As someone with very fond memories of the Yankees winning fierce, neck-and-neck Division Series battles with Oakland, Cleveland, and Baltimore over the years, I've always enjoyed a tense Game 5. One team advances to fight for the pennant while the other goes home with those hopes dashed. I don't think many neutral observers would pick either of these teams to upset the Rays after the way they posted the American League's best record in 2026 and then mopped the floor with the Yankees.

But look, all you have to do is get the next round, and you'll never know what happens. Who would've picked the 84-win Diamondbacks to upset the defending NL champion Phillies in 2023? Or going back further to a better memory for the City of Brotherly Love, how about when the 1993 Phillies dispatched a dynastic Braves team that outlasted the Giants to win 104 games? Dare to dream. The Guardians and White Sox both dared to do so; here's how the winner booked a date at Tropicana Field for ALCS Game 1 tomorrow night.

Cleveland Guardians 2, Chicago White Sox 0

Star power often wins in the playoffs, and though Cleveland isn't exactly awash with the stars the way it was in the 1990s when the team made it to multiple Fall Classics, they relied on a couple very good ones to lead the way in the winner-take-all Game 5 against the White Sox.

With a 2-0 victory, the Guardians won their third in a row, completing just the fourth comeback in MLB history for a team in a best-of-five that lost the first two games at home. To make this Yankees-centric and more familiar, this is the kind of the comeback that the 2001 Yanks pulled off against the A's, sparked by the "Flip Play" game. It's since been matched by the 2012 Giants, the 2015 Blue Jays, and now the 2026 Guardians. It's also the first 0-2 comeback of any kind in a DS since the 2017 Yanks did it to Cleveland. (Shout-out Greg Bird, Masahiro Tanaka, and Didi Gregorius.)

The two stars who took center stage for the Guardians were José Ramírez and Gavin Williams. Whenever Ramírez ends his career, he'll go down as one of the greatest players to ever wear a Cleveland uniform. October has sometimes been a struggle for him though, and he's the last remaining player from their team that lost to the Cubs in a Game 7 heartbreaker in the 2016 Fall Classic. He hasn't been back to the Greatest Stage since then, but he helped punch Cleveland's ticket to give them a shot this year by going 5-for-12 across the three ALDS wins with two homers and seven RBI.

One of those dingers came yesterday off an otherwise-solid Sean Burke, and who could blame Burke for giving up a gopher ball on a pitch this low?

Ramírez has a good shot at a plaque in Cooperstown one day and this is one of those "tip your cap" moments. Not many players can physically do that. This has actually been a tougher year for him, as he had a broken bone in his hand that forced him to miss time and ultimately ended up with a sub-100 OPS+ for the first time since 2015. If it ends in Cleveland somehow breaking its championship drought though, the man won't care a lick about his regular season.

Maybe it's overstating a bit to call Williams a star, but the 26-year-old is a dangerous up-and-coming ace for Cleveland, leading the AL with 248 strikeouts despite not making the All-Star team. The Guardians wasted his 11-K start in Game 1, but he came out of the bullpen to help nail down Game 4 when closer Cade Smith wobbled late. Under 48 hours later, Williams started the game he forced and seemed unperturbed by those 18 pitches in relief. He did one better than his playoff opener, fanning a dirty dozen White Sox in 5.2 shutout innings, allowing only a single to Kyle Teel.

Williams' primary drawback is that he doesn't go deep into games, which hurt him in Game 1. Erik Sabrowski let him down then, but he made up for it last night by relieving Williams and fanning Munetaka Murakami with the bases loaded to escape a sixth-inning jam. The 2-0 lead remained intact.

The Pale Hose never came so close to scoring again. Tristan Peters never moved after a one-out single in the seventh, as Hunter Gaddis struck out both Chase Meidroth and Colson Montgomery as the potential tying runs. Sam Antonacci singled off Gaddis with one down in the eighth, so Cleveland skipper Stephen Vogt called on Smith for a five-out save, his third appearance in four days. Despite pitching every game in this series, he was up to the task. He struck out Kyle Teel and got Miguel Vargas to foul out to end the frame, and then struck out the side in the ninth to slam the door on the Sox, who set a postseason record with 21 team strikeouts in a nine-inning game. Woof.

The White Sox deserve a ton of credit for overachieving so much in 2026 after three consecutive 100-loss seasons. No one thought they'd make the playoffs, let alone come a win shy of the ALCS. Few predicted even a .500 finish! It will hurt knowing that they had three games to close out Cleveland and instead squandered the series, but this team honestly looked about as gassed possible. Can the Guardians actually threaten the Rays? I will at least hope they put up a better fight than they did in 2024 against the Yankees.

articles.title: Godzilla Minus Zero Trailer Reveals Sneak Peek at King Ghidorah's Gravity Beams
articles.summary: Toho's latest Godzilla Minus Zero trailer is here and puts the spotlight on King Ghidorah's lightning-like gravity beams and Godzilla's iconic atomic breath.
articles.body:
Toho's latest Godzilla Minus Zero trailer is here and puts the spotlight on King Ghidorah's lightning-like gravity beams and Godzilla's iconic atomic breath.

This new sneak peek at the King of the Monsters and the latest iteration of his archnemesis debuted as part of New York Comic Con 2026. Toho refrained from showing its new design for Ghidorah yet again , but there's still plenty of new footage to see in the one-minute video.

How did Noriko Oishi (Minami Hamabe) survive Godzilla's first attack? That's the question Godzilla Minus Zero teases an answer for in its second full-length trailer. It looks like viewers are in for pure carnage this time around, as the three-headed kaiju zaps any airborne structures out of the sky left and right. You can see how the sequel's returning human crew will "fight fire with fire" next month in the trailer below.

Fight fire with fire. 🔥 #GodzillaMinusZero Godzilla Day IMAX Early Access on November 3. In theatres November 6. Tickets on sale now. — GODZILLA.OFFICIAL (@Godzilla_Toho) October 11, 2026

Fight fire with fire. 🔥 #GodzillaMinusZero Godzilla Day IMAX Early Access on November 3. In theatres November 6. Tickets on sale now.

With less than a month until its premiere, it seems the filmmakers behind the Godzilla Minus One sequel are going to save the full Ghidorah reveal for those who go to the theater. We'll at least know how the character has been redesigned for the Minus universe when it premieres November 6.

Godzilla Minus Zero's NYCC presence wasn't just limited to this electrifying new trailer, though. Producer Kazuaki Kishida, visual effects artist and compositor Tatsuji Nojima, sound designer and Foley artist Natsuko Inoue, and production and post-production sound mixer Hisafumi Takeuchi all gathered in New York for a panel covering the sequel and how it came to be. IGN attended the talk and came away with a few highlights.

Nojima, who walked away from Godzilla Minus One as the first Gen Z Oscar winner in the visual effects category, said his time working on the 2023 film started simply as a hobby before director Takashi Yamazaki took note of his abilities. Kishida joked, "I don't know if I'd have a job right now" if not for the 25-year-old VFX artist's work, but Nojima isn't the only younger member of the crew.

"There are even younger team members on the Godzilla Minus Zero team – 22, 23," Kishida said via translator. "They're talented enough to be given an entire cut or a scene to manage on their own. Director Yamazaki really likes working with young talent. I think he's very open-minded, and he absorbs whatever fresh takes or new ways younger artists are approaching different problems, and how they're solving it. There isn't really an age hierarchy in his organization. Everyone works very collaboratively, and I think it's a very good environment for young artists to try and flex what they have."

One VFX-packed scene that viewers have already caught in trailers sees Godzilla emerging from the ocean while chasing after a plane. Even short moments like this can be quite complicated to bring to life when skyscraper-sized monsters are involved. Godzilla Minus Zero's status as the first Japanese production filmed for IMAX only made the process more complex, which is why it's especially impressive that the ocean scene in question required 2 billion particles and was made by just two people.

Meanwhile, the crew had to get especially creative when trying to imagine what creatures like Godzilla and Ghidorah would sound like in real life . In Godzilla Minus One, the echo of its title kaiju's unmistakable roar was recorded by capturing audio of his voice in a baseball stadium. Introducing a new monster with Godzilla Minus Zero then took them to record audio in a dam.

"I recall there were people having a picnic, maybe people just taking a stroll," Inoue said. "The person walking their dog, though, they had the worst time because the dog was freaking out and barking back at us."

It'll all come together in just a few short weeks. In the meantime, you can see why IGN gave Godzilla Minus One an 8/10 . We've also already got a review for Godzilla Minus Zero, and you can see why we gave it a 7/10 here .

articles.title: Wildwood Sees Laika's Stop-Motion at Its Most Beautifully Epic
articles.summary: Review: Wildwood is an arresting, exciting fantasy epic made all the more impressive by the fact that it’s handmade and hand-animated, even if some story stumbles occasionally hold it back.
articles.body:
There’s something wondrous about the transportive power of stop-motion animated films when they’re executed at the standard that Laika sets for themselves, and wonder is certainly the name of the game in Wildwood. Adapted from the first novel in Colin Meloy and Carson Ellis’ Wildwood Chronicles, Wildwood sees director Travis Knight and the craftspeople at Laika turning in a staggeringly beautiful and surprisingly dark fantasy adventure that boasts exciting action, enchanting and enchanted natural settings, and talking woodland creatures with jobs… and that’s all before the characters leave Portland to journey into Wildwood!

Wildwood is most impressive in its scope. As the new recordholder for the longest-ever stop-motion animated film, Knight luxuriates in building out the mythology of Meloy and Ellis’ novels onscreen. As 13-year-old Prue McKeel (Peyton Elizabeth Lee) and her classmate Curtis (Jacob Tremblay) find themselves on a mission into the magical forest realm of Wildwood to save Prue’s kidnapped baby brother Mac, the intricate web of societies, races, and systems that prop up the setting are endlessly fascinating to keep track of thanks in large part to just how gorgeous it all looks. Laika’s films always push the boundaries of what’s possible for stop-motion animation, and the jaw-dropping artistry on display in Wildwood sees them doing it again. From the intricately authentic rendering of Portland, through each of the different domains of the massive, mystical forest, Wildwood is fathomless in its attention to fine detail.

Long stretches of the film achieve such a sense of immersion that, at its most effective, it’s easy to forget that Wildwood is a stop-motion film at all, a sensation that’s even more impressive when taking into account the wide array of fantasy trappings that Wildwood deploys.

The nature-centric magic and anthropomorphic characters Prue and Curtis come up against will no doubt feel familiar to any fans of portal fantasies like Spirited Away, Labyrinth or The Chronicles of Narnia (not to mention Laika’s own Coraline), but Knight leans into the storytelling economy afforded to him by those archetypes with confidence. The “just go with it” style of his approach to what he chooses to detail about the history of Wildwood leaves moments where the movie breezes through exposition feeling pretty inoffensive, especially in light of just how fully-realized the world feels by the end of the movie. Through it all, the stakes of the story feel very high thanks to the quickly cascading conflict Prue and Curtis’ actions set off once they cross into the wilderness. Losses feel real, setbacks have consequences and people die in this movie, and with some amount of frequency at that. At times, it’s surprising just how far Knight is willing to push the envelope for what could look on the surface like a kid-friendly romp. Sure, nothing here approaches the hellish nightmare fuel present in the R-rated, Phil Tippett-directed Mad God , but make no mistake: Wildwood more than earns its PG-13 rating.

That doesn’t stop character motivations from being occasional stumbling blocks for Wildwood, though. As fantastical and well-conceived as Wildwood’s world is, protagonist Prue does sometimes feel lost in the shuffle. Prue’s a very modern 13-year-old girl who bristles against her granola mom and dad (Maya Erskine and Jake Johnson) and takes the full brunt of responsibility for losing her brother, giving the character plenty of weight to have to shoulder as more and more bravery and pluck is required of her. Peyton Elizabeth Lee’s performance is energetic and dynamic enough to keep Prue likable, but the script doesn’t find much room for her to be more specifically defined by anything other than the wrongs she’s trying to right. That may be partially by design, maybe to let younger audience members project themselves into her adventure, but it does leave Prue feeling less memorable than the world she’s adventuring through.

The tabletop RPG-loving Curtis, still stuck on hot chocolate when his peers have moved on to coffee, plays out an expected “zero to hero” arc, with Jacob Tremblay handling the character’s comedic timing well. Wildwood’s story does take Curtis away from Prue for a lot of the movie, and the pacing tends to drag when we check back in with him and the heroic bandits he crosses paths with in enemy territory. While the record-breaking 131-minute runtime more than justifies itself from a purely visual standpoint, plot detours like this do occasionally leave Wildwood feeling a little long in the tooth.

Growing her power within Wildwood is Alexandra (Carey Mulligan), a governess of the South Wood whose grief coming out of the movie’s shockingly macabre opening scene drives her towards equally dark choices as the story goes. Alexandra’s relationship to her grief is far more interesting and believable than her machinations to quell it, but Mulligan’s quavering, edgy performance is a consistent highlight. Some late effort is made to draw parallels between Alexandra and Prue’s parents, which could’ve made Alexandra an even more compelling antagonist, but those connections don’t feel properly seeded into the early scenes to be satisfying to consider later on. From Alexandra’s grief, though, Knight does have occasion to produce some of Wildwood’s most evocative imagery, and those gothic touches are a welcome contrast to the bright, teeming life which makes up the majority of the movie’s visual identity.

What’s left to be desired by the main players is more than made up for by Wildwood’s excellently cast supporting roster of magical creatures and heroes. Mahershala Ali and Amandla Stenberg? Badass bandits! Richard E. Grant? An owl king named Owl Rex! Tom Waits? Rage-filled coyote soldier! Charlie Day? Cowardly turncoat coyote soldier! From everyone as big as Angela Bassett’s giant eagle General to as small as Awkwafina’s spunky rat Septima, the voice cast is a key aspect of Wildwood’s personality. The color each of these characters add into the mix, especially the ways the animal characters’ more base instincts peek through in their personalities, does as much to create a sense of place as any of the sun-dappled valleys or ivy-ridden ruins that Prue and Curtis traverse.

As Prue and Curtis attempt to outwit Alexandra’s forces, Wildwood’s action is breathlessly staged. The early kidnapping of the baby brother Mac by a murder of Alexandra’s crows and the chase that ensues hints at some of the gonzo camera work that’s to follow, and once the real world’s in the rear view mirror, Knight draws from every corner of his meticulously-populated frames to add a surprising twist to a fight, or to increase the danger of being caught or killed. Knight also has a pretty judicious eye for when to lock the camera into a more grounded style of coverage, and when to let it off the chain. All that excitement is very effectively supported by composer Dario Marianelli’s score, a lively orchestral bedrock which is alternatingly lead by either folk string arrangements or more modern guitar sounds depending on the environment.

articles.title: Marvel Tokon DLC Roadmap Reveals First Look at Jane Foster Thor, Venom and Jubilee Coming in 2027
articles.summary: Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls will continue its Year 1 DLC roadmap with Thor (Jane Foster) this winter, with two more characters coming in 2027.
articles.body:
Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls will continue its Year 1 DLC roadmap with Thor (Jane Foster) this winter, with two more characters coming in 2027.

Developer Arc System Works confirmed the lineup alongside Evo France 2026. The Jane Foster version of Asgard's God of Thunder is now officially set to follow Phoenix Cyclops after he releases November 2, 2026, with today's announcement coming with both a sneak peek at her Marvel Tokon model in Odin's Vault on Asgard.

The clip doesn't show too much, only teasing that we'll probably see Jane fight off Loki while wielding Mjolnir when a proper gameplay trailer premieres at a later date. Arc System Works said she's scheduled to launch in Marvel Tokon "winter 2027," so expect to see her arrival sometime before March of next year. Despite some concerns from players that poor sales could jeopardize the Marvel fighting game's future, at least two more characters will arrive in spring and summer 2027, too.

Yes, Spider-Man anti-hero and Symbiote menace Venom will finally join the roster in spring 2027. X-Men firecracker Jubilee will then follow in the summer of that year. While Cyclops and Thor are entering the fray as relatively lesser-known versions of themselves, Venom and Jubilee appear to be mostly straightforward.

That means Marvel Tokon players will get to see them fight the rest of the tag-team fighting with and against the game's roster – which includes characters like Doctor Doom, Iron Man, Carnage, Magneto, and more – in Arc System Works' heightened style. Although the details surrounding each DLC release are unclear, the reveal trailer did at least confirm that Venom will also come with a stage based on the Symbiote home world of Klyntar.

It's all part of the Year 1 Character and Stage Pass, which costs $34.99. A roadmap with some of the most beloved characters from Marvel history would usually be enough to have comic book and video game fans frothing at the mouth, but uncertainty surrounding the project might have some looking at the Evo announcement in a different light.

Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls Knights of Doom State of Play June 2026 Reveal Trailer - Screenshots

Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls launched to strong reviews (a 9/10 from IGN) in August, but at least on PC, players have struggled. Its Steam launch brought mixed reviews from fans who complained of widespread technical issues and PlayStation Network requirements. Even as the developers almost immediately promised to investigate the issues, it didn't take long for the backlash to swell to the point that famed fighting game community member Maximilian Dood wrote off playing the PC version altogether .

It only took a few days for Arc System Works to push out a fix for most players' issues , but as Steam player numbers still struggle to break even 1,000 concurrent users (via SteamDB ), even the developers have admitted earning back trust will be "extremely challenging." While Marvel Tokon's presence on PlayStation 5 seemed to go over well, director Kazuto Sekine eventually went on to apologize for the PC launch .

The developers clearly have a game plan for at least up until summer 2027. While we wait to see how characters like Thor, Venom, and Jubilee will punch and kick their way into Marvel Tokon, you can read about the characters dataminers were expecting to see first .
