articles.title: ‘I’m Shocked That People Are Still Playing’ – How GTA 5 Took Over the World
articles.summary: Could GTA 6 be as big as its predecessor? We take a look at how GTA 5 became one of the biggest games in history, selling over 230m copies and being played by millions of people every week for over a decade.
articles.body:
There are over 230 million copies of Grand Theft Auto 5 in the world. As the second-highest selling game of all time, it has been played for billions of hours by players across the globe, making it one of the most significant pastimes in the entire world. That’s an impressive achievement for what in 2013 was simply the highly-anticipated next entry in Rockstar’s beloved (and notorious) open-world crime series. But GTA 5 proved to be much, much more than a typical sequel. It has become home to a huge, expressive, and loyal community, one which has made a digital hobby of everything from warring alien clans to producing slick vehicle stunt movies.

This is the story of how a video game became much more than a crime simulator.

Ash Skyqueen’s avatar weaves between the traffic of busy Dorset Drive on a motorbike spouting flames. Suddenly she veers, mounting the pavement at high speed and rebounding from the roof of a bus stop to achieve incredible air. Momentum carries her through a perfect circle, barely bigger than a human body, that forms the second ‘O’ of the ‘LIQUOR HOLE’ store sign. Pulling the ripcord of her parachute, she lands with a slight stagger at the door of the rundown booze establishment on Eclipse Boulevard - a couple of streets over from where her jump began.

It’s the first feat in a stunt montage which Ash put together to celebrate ten years of GTA 5 – the game that gave her freedom, companionship and goals when she was robbed of all three. “I’d had a ruptured disc in my spine, so I was bed bound shortly after the game came out,” she says. “All day every day for about three years straight, it became my therapy in a way. You’re stuck in bed, can’t do anything, can’t work, no social life, a pretty miserable existence. And then I’m suddenly connected to a community of people doing the same thing. It kept me from going insane.”

It’s a striking demonstration of why GTA 5 has remained a deeply important game to millions of players. A pillar of pop culture, it was erected in 2013 and has loomed over the entertainment industries during every year since. Thanks to the enduring love for its single-player story campaign and its ever-popular, seemingly invincible online mode, GTA 5 has spanned three console generations and made around $10 billion dollars for publisher Take-Two – over 3 times more than the highest-grossing movie ever. When Shawn Levy and Ryan Reynolds made Free Guy, a Hollywood comedy about the social connection and wanton violence of online games, it was GTA they chose to riff on.

Where previous Grand Theft Auto entries were cinema-riffing crime simulators that routinely broke sales records, GTA 5 has evolved beyond those confines. It has become an alternate world where players can escape to a funhouse mirror version of LA – the most mythologised city on the planet. There they become whoever they want to be: stunt specialist, bank robber, nightclub kid, hitchhiker or filmmaker.

In some ways, GTA 5 was a course correction for Rockstar. While 2008’s Grand Theft Auto 4 had been rapturously received, it was a narrower interpretation of what the series could be. Some players chafed against its dour and grounded tone, as well as the unforgiving driving simulation that threatened to hurl speeding players through the windscreen. It was a largely straight-faced vision that left a space for rivals like Saints Row developer Volition, who filled the vacuum with gleefully absurd city sandboxes populated by dildo-toting gangsters and gimp chariots.

GTA 5, however, saw Rockstar reclaim its lost territory in the single-player space without compromising its serious storytelling chops. The developer turned up all the dials on its screaming satire, filling its campaign missions with ludicrous plane, train, and helicopter setpieces in which the bodies hit the floor without moral consequence. The driving was made friendlier, and the oppressive skyscrapers of GTA 4 replaced by the open freeways of the San Andreas countryside. Yet GTA 5 also told the ambitious tale of three controllable protagonists at totally different points in their lives – Franklin, the young and hungry Scarface-in-waiting; Michael, the washed-up cuckold; and Trevor, the psychopathic embodiment of the five-star Wanted level.

As clear as that ambition is to see in the final product, Mike York had nothing close to a sense of that full picture when he first joined the GTA 5 development team as an animator, two and a half years before its launch.

“A lot of times during production you’re thrown in there, and you don’t know what the story is and how it plays out,” he says. “There are a lot of scenes where I didn’t even know what came before or after. I was so out of the loop with the story of the game. They just threw me a cutscene with Tanisha and Franklin and were like, ‘Hey, can you do the body animation on this?’ But I had no idea how it connected. All I knew is, ‘Damn, this girl looks mad at Franklin. She looks like she just broke up with him.’”

Even in the final six months of development, when members of the team were “all hands on deck” and testing the game for eight hours every day, it was impossible to perceive GTA 5 in its entirety.

“As a tester, you’re trying to play through the whole game over and over and over again,” York says. “But the game is very long. A lot of times I would play the game from the very beginning, up until 60% or 70%, and then a new build of the game would come out where they fixed a bunch of bugs. And so I only played the game from start to finish all the way one time, and that was after I was done from the project and played it at my house by myself.”

Only then could York finally appreciate the enormous puzzle he’d been contributing pieces to for so long. “I think the biggest thing I was shocked about was how massive it was, how big the world was, and how cool the system was of being able to switch characters,” he says. “I thought that was unique, and I knew that players hadn’t seen that before.” It’s a system that Rockstar’s peers in the triple-A sphere are only now catching up to - infusing Spider-Man 2 and Assassin’s Creed Shadows with swappable protagonists whose stories are entwined.

As an American, York appreciated Rockstar North’s Scottish perspective - an outsider’s view of the quirks and comedy inherent in LA culture. “I think they have a pretty good eye, a good touch on our society,” he says. “And that’s because, even though the main studio is in Edinburgh, a lot of the people that work there are from the US, or all they do is watch US TV shows and play US games. They’re engulfed in our culture in general. So even though they live in the UK, they have a good pulse on everything that’s going around here.”

When the midnight launch came, Ash Skyqueen and her sister stood in line at the Metrocentre shopping mall in the north-east of England. Like so many others, she took the game home and pushed it straight into the console. Behind the scenes, the development team were “stoked, walking around the office and telling people, ‘Oh my God, did you see we just sold this many?’ There were a lot of funny comments from people on YouTube channels and we were all geeking out about that.”

Simultaneously, however, Rockstar was readying to launch GTA Online - the platform that would take Los Santos multiplayer. “We were trying to get prepared for that, too,” York says. “So half of it is excitement, and the other half is trying to get some stuff done for Online.”

GTA Online arrived only two weeks after its parent game and immediately ran into problems. There were difficulties with servers, crashes and lost character progress. The IGN review of the time criticised the repetitive missions and oddly mute player avatars, who contributed little to cutscenes with established GTA characters like Trevor. “I’m left with the overbearing impression,” wrote Keza MacDonald, “that Grand Theft Auto Online as it stands right now is still a colour sketch of what it will probably one day become.”

In 2017, Rockstar’s then director of design, Imran Sarwar, offered an unusually frank assessment of GTA Online’s formative period. “To be totally honest it did not begin very well at all,” he told Game Informer . “It’s one of our biggest regrets that we lost millions of players in that first year that have never experienced how much we have improved and added to the game since the early days.”

Rockstar had promised players cooperative heists – huge multistage missions featuring lavish story sequences in the mode of single-player GTA. But the company’s first attempts didn’t live up to its own standards and had to be redesigned from scratch, leading to several delays.

“GTA Online was slowly failing - and quickly losing players - right up until the middle of 2014,” Sarwar said. “The updates were not interesting enough, and as a company we did not realise how challenging it was going to be to have a team that essentially ran a content service, not make normal games.”

This is not the obvious oversight it might seem today. When GTA Online launched, the live service model was in its nascency. Fortunately, as Rockstar fumbled around trying to figure out the shape of its multiplayer platform, it had a critically acclaimed single-player game to lean on. “GTA 5 helped prop up GTA Online in the early days when Rockstar was still exploring how it wanted the online component to work,” says James McWhirter, senior games analyst at Omdia. “There was a lot of experimentation going on behind the scenes.”

Some of those experiments were in economics. If there’s a comparison to be drawn, it’s Team Fortress 2 – the competitive FPS that Valve used as a testing ground for new business models that have since become standard in Counter-Strike, Dota 2, and a host of other games besides. Ultimately, GTA 5 has made its billions through multiple different methods.

“It’s simultaneously pulling all of those levers,” McWhirter says. “You’ve got the upfront sales for GTA 5 itself, the full game. You’ve got in-game purchases via GTA Online, and now Rockstar have begun to lean into subscriptions with GTA+.”

None of that would have panned out if the GTA Online team hadn’t solved its biggest creative problem: heists. As Rockstar began to update its world with unique new stories and complex missions that demanded coordination and mastery from their players, GTA Online genuinely started to look like the future of the series rather than a flawed spin-off. Even resolutely solo players braved the servers for fear of being left behind.

“I was kind of shocked by how much extra story and missions they put into Online,” York says, who left Rockstar in 2017 – a few years before the likes of the Cayo Perico and Diamond Casino heists were added. “They really went all out, I felt, adding all kinds of stuff to do in there.”

GTA Online’s turnaround and subsequent financial success came at the cost of single-player expansions. Actor Steven Ogg filmed scenes for a solo campaign that would have featured Trevor as an undercover agent, but it never emerged thanks to GTA Online sucking up many of the resources once earmarked for DLC.

“I can’t speak for the company, obviously,” York says. “But I think that they wanted to do a little bit of both. And I think they did have strong intent with DLC stuff, but the Online just did better. That happens a lot at studios, where they’ll have a DLC lined up that they’ll have plans for, and then they’ll completely shut it down because they realise something else is way more important - or they don’t even know if that DLC is going to perform well at all. They’d rather just not take the risk on it.”

GTA Online effectively took the place of traditional expansions, becoming an endgame for solo players who had exhausted every mission and diversion in GTA 5. Unusually for newcomers to an MMO, they arrived with dozens of hours of investment in its world and characters. “You know the map and where the streets are,” York says. “You finally get your own character.”

“I played it like a single-player expansion at first,” Ash Skyqueen says. “Played through everything I could by myself, and kept playing. The mechanics have always been what appeals, so it was easy to sit there and figure out what I could do.”

It’s with this spirit of exploration that GTA’s developers and players outgrew the limitations of the series’ original premise. “The more comfortable we were pushing beyond the traditional GTA concepts and experimenting more freely, we were able to introduce things like Cunning Stunts, the Special Vehicle Races, and adversary modes like Power Play, Tiny Racers, or Slasher,” Sarwar told Game Informer .

The backdrop of Los Santos, recognisable as a contemporary city only slightly adjacent to our own world, proved helpfully malleable. “One of the updates GTA Online brought in was a TrackMania style game, racing in the cloud with a top-down perspective, almost like Micro Machines,” McWhirter says. “That just wouldn’t have been possible in Red Dead Redemption. Anything with a real world analog can be realised in GTA Online, so it’s a much more potent canvas for content updates over a long period of time. Whereas Red Dead is a lot more tied to its fiction. You couldn’t have flying horses, like having flying cars added to GTA Online.”

That flexibility has enabled Rockstar to transform GTA into a platform for many different kinds of experiences, capable of holding player attention indefinitely. “Similar to Minecraft or Fortnite, it’s a virtual world first and foremost, and a game second,” McWhirter says. “In terms of GTA Online, the racing updates with the crazy track editors are a good example of how content that could perhaps normally make for a standalone game became a bolt-on for GTA Online.”

Over time, these bolt-ons have replaced smaller game releases in Rockstar’s catalogue, for better or worse. “I would consider GTA Online to be the modern day equivalent of the double-A titles that Take-Two used to push out between those blockbuster games,” McWhirter says. “If we go back to the PS3 and 360 generation, there were games like Rockstar Games Presents Table Tennis and Bully, which we don’t really see anymore because teams are busy making content for GTA Online instead. Because that’s more valuable for the publisher. It helps them buy time between major GTA releases.”

For players like Ash Skyqueen, a new content drop in GTA Online serves a dual purpose. Beyond the extra heists and missions to play through, every update is a toy box filled with fresh animations and props to be repurposed in fan-made movies.

Skyqueen got into making machinima through her community of stunters, who made use of a modding tool named MenyooSP. “It gives you access to everything,” she says. “I can set up a secondary character, give it a list of actions and animations to carry out, and then manually control my character and do what I need to do.”

In her own movies, Skyqueen is star, stuntperson and director - the latter role enabled by the official video editor Rockstar added to GTA 5 back in 2015. One of her most popular creations, the silent short film Siren , evokes the intro cutscene of GTA 3 – following a Bonnie and Clyde-esque couple who wreak havoc as the FIB closes in. In the climax, a pre-programmed prison bus travels down the freeway - before Ash swings in on her bike to take down the convoy.

“There’s a lot of choreography involved,” she says. “I’ll often just sit there with a nine-hour long YouTube video of all the GTA story cutscenes, keeping my eye out for something that I can use in a different context.”

180,000 viewers have watched Siren. Almost a million people have watched her Liqour Hole stunt . And Skyqueen hopes Rockstar will implement some of MenyooSP’s innovations officially in GTA 6. “I know they take note of this kind of stuff, and they certainly have promoted work that’s been made with it.”

The ongoing success of GTA 5 raises questions about its eventual fate, once Rockstar’s sequel launches in November 2026. Will the studio run two versions of GTA Online simultaneously, at the risk of cannibalising its own playerbase? If not, and the GTA Online audience is migrated to a new Floridian setting, how will Rockstar account for all the properties and vehicles players have paid for?

“If a new online mode is a completely separate thing from GTA 5 Online, managing continuously between two live service games is something that is currently unproven and it could be fraught,” McWhirter says. “I think that’s probably the biggest risk for them.” The situation brings to mind the arrival of EverQuest 2 in the mid noughties, when developer Sony Online Entertainment discovered that players typically played just one MMO and stuck with it. In such a context, a sequel’s biggest threat can be its own predecessor.

“I think GTA 5 is going to solidify as one of the greatest games in history,” York says. “I think its legacy is already etched. It was revolutionary in so many aspects - in character switching and story. I’m shocked that people are still playing GTA 5, and it goes to show you how good that game is.”

While admitting to a certain amount of bias as a former member of the development team, York believes that GTA 5 will be bigger than its own sequel once the dust settles. “I feel like GTA 5 was something special in gaming culture and history, and it’s gonna leave a lasting mark,” he says. “Games will come and go around it. My intuition is that GTA 6 will come out, people will love it, but it won’t be GTA 5. And people will constantly compare it to GTA 5. It’s going to be the most nostalgic for people, it’s going to be the one that affected them most as kids. And so I just feel like GTA 5 is going to be the GTA to be remembered. It’s gonna supersede Vice City. This is the one that marked history.”

For Ash Skyqueen, who can no longer drive around a city in real life, GTA 5 is much more than a game. “It gives me that little bit of freedom back that I lost with the injury,” she says. “Though it’s simulated, it has such a good feel to it. I’ll always get on at Christmas when they turn on the snow. You’re walking around the streets at night, and it gives you that same vibe as in real life. In other games it’s just an aesthetic. But you can feel that stillness that comes with a dark snowy night. I don’t know how they do it.”

Jeremy Peel is a freelance journalist and friend to anyone who will look at photos of his dogs.

articles.title: Tekken 8 Yujiro Teaser Reveals Baki Rep's In-Game Render Is Just as Uncanny as Fans Expected
articles.summary: Bandai Namco has revealed a first look at Tekken 8 DLC character Yujiro Hanma, and the Baki rep is looking just as uncanny as fans expected.
articles.body:
Bandai Namco has revealed a first look at Tekken 8 DLC character Yujiro Hanma, and the Baki rep is looking just as uncanny as fans expected.

The new trailer for the fighting game's Season 3 characters debuted alongside Evo France 2026. Following Kunimitsu's release in June and Bob's release in August, kangaroo-and-joey fighter Roger Jr. is now officially set for a November 11 early access launch, with the full release following November 16, but the character most fans are looking forward to is still without a proper release date.

Roger Jr. is definitely the star of the new Tekken 8 DLC trailer, with nearly three minutes of its four-minute runtime dedicated to showing off the marsupial boxer's gameplay. The Yujiro teaser, meanwhile, is tucked at the end, but its reveals are particularly shocking. You can see how the Baki the Grappler villain has been reimagined within the world of Tekken below.

Yujiro is… expressive, to say the least, so nailing his face and bulging muscles was always going to draw attention. Well, the Bandai Namco team did their best, with today's Evo trailer showing just a few shots of his iconic toothy smile and flexibility.

It looks like work on the anime guest character is still underway, but just because there's no release date doesn't mean there isn't a plan to show more. The end of the new teaser promised that a new Yujiro trailer will premiere alongside the Tekken World Tour Finals January 17, 2027. That's three months out from now, so we can probably expect to see gameplay by that point.

Looking back at the calendar, Bandai Namco has typically had a few months of downtime between Tekken 8 DLC releases. It will have been two months since Roger Jr. was released when the Yujiro trailer is shared, meaning we can also expect a release date announcement around that time, too. If we're lucky, the Baki fighter might even drop that same day, but again, nothing regarding his release date has been confirmed quite yet.

Tekken 8 Clive Character Trailer Screenshots

Roger Jr. and Yujiro are both included in the Season 3 pass and will round out its promise of four bonus characters. Season 1 and Season 2 included fighters like Heihachi, Armor King, Anna, and Final Fantasy 16 protagonist Clive Rosfield. While passes cost $30 each, the Season 3 pass is currently available for $34.99.

IGN learned more about Yujiro's inclusion in Tekken 8 when speaking with producer Naoya Yasuda and director of promotions and former Baki manga editor Yuki Yokoi earlier this year. Be sure to read the full interview for insight into how and why the team decided to include a character that never loses. You can also read about how former Tekken director Katsuhiro Harada influenced one of Roger Jr.'s best references , and the player who climbed through the ranks while blindfolded .

articles.title: Down SFC: Clonduff beat Burren to end 26-year wait for Frank O'Hare Cup
articles.summary: Clonduff end a 26-year wait for the Down SFC title with a 1-14 to 1-10 victory over Burren at Pairc Esler.
articles.body:
Clonduff ended 26 years of hurt to finally get their hands back on the Frank O'Hare Cup with a 1-14 to 1-10 win over Burren in the Down Senior Football Championship final at Pairc Esler.

It was a cagey affair across the hour in Newry as both sides bid for county glory, Burren losing their third final in four years as Clonduff prevailed in their first decider appearance since 2016.

The Mourne county has been under the stranglehold of Kilcoo dominance for what feels like an eternity, with this final the first without the Magpies in 15 years, as their bid for eight titles in a row was halted by Burren in the last four.

As both sides looked to impose themselves, it was captain Charlie Carr's goal that gave the men in yellow an early advantage.

A couple of two-point frees from Eamon Brown ensured a 1-6 to 0-4 lead at the break, and the forward put the success down to the words of Mayo All-Ireland winning boss Andy Moran.

"I was actually listening to Andy Moran's podcast during the week, and just one thing he said, just don't stop swinging whatever happens, just keep shooting and just keep shooting," Brown told BBC Sport NI.

"It's unbelievable. The fans throughout the whole game were actually unbelievable, we had a 16th man, any time we scored, the roar was just incredible. Any time Burren made a mistake, it was our roar.

"You know, finals...you can think of the occasion or whatever, but our whole thing was, as long as we work harder than them, we want it more than them. That's what it comes down to, and that's what we've done."

'You can see what it means to so many people'

Carr's goal was a real captain's contribution to settle any early nerves, while his composure was key as Niall Toner's 41st-minute goal threatened to stir a comeback.

"It's very hard to put into words, you can see what it means to so many people. It feels like there's thousands and thousands out on the field here," Carr told BBC Sport NI.

"Just to finally get over the line, it's more a sense of relief because I feel we've probably left a couple behind in the last few years. I mean, finals are just all about winning and thankfully we did that today.

"You know, it's ten years since we were in a final and I think there's seven people playing that are involved today that were involved then. So, caginess was probably to be expected.

"The first week back after the Carryduff game in the semi-final, training was cagey. So, maybe training translated right on to the field. But nerves are normal. No matter how cagey it was, I'm just glad we came out to the right side of it."

The season does not end here for Clonduff. They will now go to represent the county in the Ulster Club Championship, starting with a preliminary clash against the Tyrone winners on the weekend ending the 1 November.

Their opponents will be known after next Sunday's Red Hand decider, where Errigal Ciaran take on an Edendork side appearing in their first senior final.

"I was reminded there of an Ulster campaign that never came into anybody's head. So, it'll be back down there on Wednesday night. Get back to the tactics board and ready to go," said Carr.

"It's a massive honour. A massive honour for me and Stephen (McConville) to be up there on behalf of our players lifting the Cup.

"But to represent the county in Ulster is a massive honour for the whole group. Hopefully, we can give it a bit of a run, we'll take it one game at a time. The Tyrone Champions come out flying in Ulster, it's bonus territory for us."

articles.title: New NetEase FPS Sparks Warzone 'Rip-Off' Claims, But Some Call of Duty Fans Are Happy to See It
articles.summary: Call of Duty fans are torn about NetEase Games' ECC: Redline, a new FPS that many have called a "rip-off" with the power to fill the void for frustrated Warzone players.
articles.body:
Call of Duty fans are torn about NetEase Games' ECC: Redline, a new FPS that many have called a "rip-off" with the power to fill the void for frustrated Warzone players.

NetEase called its new shooter a "self-developed extreme-sports tactical shooter" when revealing it just days ago. It's yet another big swing from the China-based tech company that boasts breakneck gameplay on PC via Steam and mobile devices, but in the hours since its big debut, it's also been called a "1:1 rip" of Activision's Call of Duty: Warzone, and it's not too hard to see why.

Viewers say guns look, kick, and move in a way that seems familiar, but the similarities don't stop there. Everything down the UI is being investigated by FPS enjoyers, too, with things like the sound effects also evoking the same kind of gritty action Call of Duty is known for. Even the way the first-person camera blurs when dropping from heights might feel familiar to fans of Warzone and other shooters. Even with characters that present their own unique abilities and gadgets, ECC: Redline has had a hard time escaping the comparisons online.

Introducing ECC: REDLINE, an extreme-sports tactical shooter. Welcome to the Extreme Circuit Championship. Enter the Circuit, Own the Edge. Wishlist now on Steam: #ECCREDLINE #ECC — ECC (@ECCREDLINE) October 9, 2026

Introducing ECC: REDLINE, an extreme-sports tactical shooter. Welcome to the Extreme Circuit Championship. Enter the Circuit, Own the Edge. Wishlist now on Steam: #ECCREDLINE #ECC

"Warzone + Delta Force + Blood Strike = ECC: Redline," one YouTube comment left on NetEase's official upload said .

"It’s 1-to-1 Warzone, hilarious s**t," another commenter on Reddit said .

"Literally the first thing that popped into my head was wow they have no shame," another replied , "straight copied COD even down to the UI and emblems etc."

Meanwhile, Call of Duty has faced its own struggles in the six years since the Call of Duty: Modern Warfare reboot introduced Warzone in 2019. Like so many other popular ongoing FPS experiences, the battle royale offshoot's popularity has ebbed and flowed, with many of its millions of fans often still calling back to its launch build and its first map, Verdansk, as the glory days.

This looks about as close of a 1:1 rip of Warzone as someone could legally get away with — ModernWarzone (@ModernWarzone) October 9, 2026

This looks about as close of a 1:1 rip of Warzone as someone could legally get away with

This is Warzone with player abilities and some blatant CoD rips😂 — Jake Lucky (@JakeSucky) October 10, 2026

This is Warzone with player abilities and some blatant CoD rips😂

@iKaito_1 similar? its literally copy and paste — 👾 (@Axie_Umami) October 9, 2026

@iKaito_1 similar? its literally copy and paste

Activision has returned to Verdansk in an attempt to recapture that magic , but it's done little to calm those nostalgic for the past. As the broader Call of Duty brand goes through its own struggles , some players – even those willing to admit NetEase may have gone too far in a few places – say a polished-looking shooter like ECC: Redline could scratch a pretty specific itch. Some even believe the NetEase shooter could give Call of Duty a run for its money.

"If ECC: Redline actually has good servers, movement, AND listens to its community… COD might finally have to start trying again," one post on X/Twitter said .

"Close enough, welcome back OG Warzone," another player said , acknowledging the similarities before saying the NetEase game "looks better tbh."

Looks like someone reverse-engineered OG Warzone and added character abilities. I’m actually kinda interested in trying this 😅 — Westie (@MrProWestie) October 10, 2026

Looks like someone reverse-engineered OG Warzone and added character abilities. I’m actually kinda interested in trying this 😅

Warzone don’t have ability 🥳! Netease definitely might pull this one off lol — Ju banks (@banks_ju) October 9, 2026

Warzone don’t have ability 🥳! Netease definitely might pull this one off lol

@ModernWarzone So what? I'd rather spend it on a ripoff game who listens to their customers then a conglomerate who 💩 on them. — 𝗥𝗶𝗴 𝕏 (@RigTate) October 10, 2026

@ModernWarzone So what? I'd rather spend it on a ripoff game who listens to their customers then a conglomerate who 💩 on them.

"I LEGIT thought it was WZ at first because i didn't check the title," one social media user said , adding a crying emoji.

NetEase has faced criticism regarding its approach to previous games in the past. A less extreme example is Marvel Rivals , a comic book hero shooter that exploded with popularity – and also managed to pick up some comparisons to Blizzard Entertainment's Overwatch – when it launched in 2024. On the other hand is Hyper Front, a 5v5 tactical shooter that Riot Games launched a lawsuit against after it drew comparisons to Valorant.

ECC: Redline currently has no release date but is being billed as a free-to-play game. Warzone, meanwhile, is slated to receive a slew of new updates when Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 launches later this month.

articles.title: Resident Evil Overtakes Weapons as Zach Cregger's Highest-Grossing Film, The Social Reckoning Bombs
articles.summary: Resident Evil beat Weapons to become Zach Cregger's highest-grossing film while The Social Reckoning bombed at the box office.
articles.body:
Resident Evil beat Weapons to become director Zach Cregger's highest-grossing film while The Social Reckoning bombed at the box office.

The live-action adaptation of Capcom's classic survival horror series turned heads as it reached an estimated worldwide total of $320.2 million over the weekend. With $138.5 million domestically and $181.7 million internationally, Resident Evil has officially cleared Weapons' $270 million with a few weeks and change to spare.

Cregger brought his re-imagined Raccoon City to the big screen on September 18, 2026, making this weekend its fourth in theaters. The massive jump – which saw it return to the number one spot, globally – was largely propelled by its premiere in China. Of the whopping $62.65 million it accumulated through weekend four, $40.6 million was earned in China alone. Its victory over Weapons already seemed secure, but as it stands atop Cregger's catalog, it's also continuing to leave its reported $75 million budget in the dust.

Resident Evil's ongoing success in theaters kicked off when it brought in $108.3 million in its opening weekend. It was a strong start that even managed to bleed over into the gaming world with increased sales for some of the games, too, with Cregger's latest also landing as the highest-rated video game adaptation of all time.

It's hard to imagine the film's release going any better than it did, especially considering the months leading up to its premiere were plagued by negativity online. Gaming fans spent much of their time talking about the movie's lack of recognizable characters and its tweaks to the lore, with Cregger arguing that he made the changes in order to make a better movie . By just about every measure, it seems the bet paid off.

These mid-October box office results show signs of an audience ready for Halloween, with Other Mommy also performing well despite poor reviews from both critics and audiences alike (via Rotten Tomatoes ). Sitting with an abysmal 18% critic score and 47% audience score, Jessica Chastain's new horror movie landed in second place globally with 45.19 million (27.5 million domestically, $17.69 million internationally).

As bone-chilling trailers convinced scary movie fans to show up for an unnerving performance, there were also some notable losers in theaters, too. Tom Cruise's Digger continued its unfortunate run with $9.6 million in weekend two, marking a 48% drop for a total of $35.3 million. The true disappointment, though, was Aaron Sorkin's The Social Network sequel, The Social Reckoning.

Starring Jeremy Allen White and Mikey Madison, and including Jeremy Strong's performance as Mark Zuckerberg, the film's opening weekend saw it open in seventh place with just $9 million. At $5.5 million domestically and $17.69 million internationally on a reported budget of $30 million (via Variety ), The Social Reckoning is a certified bomb.

It's a painful reality for the Facebook movie follow-up, especially after Jesse Eisenberg's original picture ended its run with $224.9 million (via Box Office Mojo ) and plenty of praise. The Social Reckoning could always stand the test of time, but with a Rotten Tomatoes score of 55% from critics and 74% from audiences, it's not looking good.

The 25 Best Body Horror Movies of All Time

October still has plenty to give, though. Capcom's live-action Street Fighter movie and Nathan Fielder's You Can See Everything will both release next weekend, October 16. DC body horror movie Clayface then follows October 23.

For the movies you can see in theaters now, be sure to check out IGN's reviews. We called Resident Evil "Great" with an 8/10 and Other Mommy "Bad" with a 4/10 . We talked about the highs and lows of Digger in our 6/10 review for the Cruise film, while The Social Reckoning returned a 7/10 .

articles.title: Artemis Fowl Animated TV Show Greenlit With Eoin Colfer as Executive Producer
articles.summary: Artemis Fowl is coming back to TV screens in the form of an animated show on Disney Channel and Disney+.
articles.body:
Artemis Fowl is coming back to TV screens in the form of an animated show on Disney Channel and Disney+.

Author Eoin Colfer announced that Disney had greenlit another series project based on his family fantasy novels at the 25 Years of Artemis Fowl panel at New York Comic Con 2026. He'll remain involved in the animated show as an executive producer, too, with Disney promising that he'll bring "his creative vision to dig deeper into the characters and lore of the beloved book series that is celebrating its 25th anniversary of the first book this year."

Joining Colfer in the executive producing category is Marvel's Moon Girl and Devil Dinosaur's Ben Juwono, as well as DuckTales' Colleen Evanson. In a statement, the Artemis Fowl author said he is "proud and delighted to be part of the formidable team that is putting the Artemis Fowl animation on screen."

"Everyone is so talented and so positive that I feel certain the fairy world is in excellent hands," he added.

The Artemis Fowl animated series has no release date, but when it does eventually arrive, it won't be the first swing at the property to land on Disney+. In 2020, Disney launched a live-action movie with the same name , though it largely failed to leave a good impression on fans or critics. As recorded by review aggregator Rotten Tomatoes , the straight-to-streaming film only whipped up a "rotten" 8% from critics and 19% from audiences.

The Artemis Fowl movie starred Ferdia Shaw as its title character and also featured appearances from Lara McDonnell, Josh Gadd, and Michael Rouse. IGN called it "an empty science fantasy tale with forgettable characters and an uninspired story" in our 4/10 review . In other words, a crack at a film didn't quite pan out, but where the 2020 project failed, the new animated show hopes to succeed.

"The action-adventure fantasy series Artemis Fowl follows 13-year-old genius Artemis Fowl as he uncovers an underground world of armed and dangerous — and surprisingly high-tech — fairies as he launches a plan to capture one and steal its magic to heal his dying mom and save his family," a description said.

The original Artemis Fowl book was published in 2001, with the rest of Colfen's stories in the universe boasting more than 35 million copies sold across the globe. Elsewhere at NYCC 2026, we got another solid look at both Godzilla Minus Zero and Blade Runner 2099 . More Naruto was confirmed to be on the way , too.

articles.title: Doom 2016 Composer Mick Gordon Says He'd Return to the Doom Series "In a Heartbeat"
articles.summary: Doom 2016 Composer Mick Gordon Says He'd Return to the Doom Series "In a Heartbeat"
articles.body:
Mick Gordon, the legendary Aussie composer who brought a headbang to every headshot in 2016's Doom and its 2020 follow-up Doom Eternal, has told IGN that he's open to the idea of contributing to future instalments in id Software's iconic shooter series. During an interview conducted at this weekend's PAX Australia, Gordon seemed to indicate that his involvement with Doom isn't necessarily done for good, despite the very public falling-out that occurred between the composer and Doom Eternal's development team in the wake of its release.

"There are a lot of dominoes that would have to fall in a very specific way for that to occur," said Gordon. "If those dominoes ever fell in that way, I would. Of course. Within a heartbeat."

Gordon didn't elaborate on exactly what those "dominoes" might be, but it's possible that disputes between the composer and Doom Eternal's executive producer Marty Stratton have yet to be fully resolved. In a lengthy 2022 post on Medium , Gordon accused developer id Software of failing to pay him for half of his work on the Doom Eternal soundtrack, and singled out Stratton as being a recurringly abusive presence throughout his work on the score and the OST. However, it certainly seems as though the experience hasn't dimmed Gordon's love for Doom itself.

"I had a whole list of ideas where I wanted to go with Doom," explained Gordon. "And I'd love to explore that one day, for sure."

What the future of Doom looks like with or without Gordon's involvement is another story. id Software was one of the many studios heavily impacted by Microsoft's ongoing cuts to its Xbox business, with 136 members of staff at the Doom developer affected by layoffs in July. At the time, lead services programmer Chris Hays was quoted as saying, "It's hard to make a game that is AAA, that's like we've done before, with half the people. And by hard, I mean impossible."

In the meantime, Gordon has been keeping busy with a variety of projects. He's contributed the theme music for the final boss fight in Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun 2, which will be released on October 14. He's also still actively at work producing the full soundtrack for Defect, the squad-based cyberpunk shooter developed by veterans of Doom and the Call of Duty series. In 2027, he's set to return to Doom at least in a performance sense, as the headliner at the UK's RADAR music festival where he'll be performing the music he composed for Doom and Doom Eternal with a full live band for the first time.

articles.title: Doom 2016 Composer Mick Gordon Says "F##k AI"
articles.summary: Doom 2016 Composer Mick Gordon Says "F##k AI"
articles.body:
Aussie composer Mick Gordon is highly regarded for his experimental approach to musical composition. For 2013's Killer Instinct he employed a kangling, a Tibetan instrument traditionally carved into a human femur or tibia, to build a theme for the skeletal Spinal character out of actual bones. For 2016's Doom he famously sampled real chainsaw noises to pull off the unique guitar riffs that elevated the game's soundtrack into a heavy metal masterpiece. However, when asked if he's considered incorporating any form of generative AI into his creative process, Gordon doesn't mince his words. To paraphrase the late Meatloaf, Gordon will do anything to create a great soundtrack, but he won't do that .

"F##k AI," said Gordon, during an interview with IGN at PAX Australia 2026.

Gordon can next be heard in Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun 2 when it's released on October 14, since he's contributed another bone-shattering banger to score the first-person shooter's final boss fight (which you can get a taste of in the trailer below). He's also still hard at work on the soundtrack to Defect, the cyberpunk-themed squad-shooter that's being developed by a team composed of veterans of the Doom and Call of Duty games. Fans can rest assured that in both instances, Gordon's music is coming straight from the metal-loving maestro's mind (and fingers) rather than the result of a ChatGPT prompt.

"Generative AI is always going to be behind where humans are because it's going to be inherently trained off stuff that humans have already created," explained Gordon. "It creates a large database of what [it's] been trained on, and then it draws a very logical conclusion on whatever that dataset is. It's always going to be limited by its dataset, though. It's never going to be in a state where it's going to predict the next thing, the new thing, whatever humans can come up with. It's always going to be behind just by the nature of the way that these things work."

Gordon remains optimistic that audiences are always going to be drawn to the work of other humans, rather than machines.

"Humans are always going to want to interact with other humans. Always," said Gordon. "And I feel this AI stuff is just giving people more reason to abandon this digital infection that we have with our lives now."

"I feel that humans are always going to chase that human connection."

UK-based fans of Gordon's work will be able to make a human connection with the man himself when he takes the stage as the headline act at 2027's RADAR festival , where he is set to perform music from his Doom and Doom Eternal soundtracks live with a full band for the very first time.

articles.title: How loud, exactly, was the Brewers crowd for Game 1?
articles.summary: Here's how loud the American Family Field crowd got for big moments in Game 1 against the Dodgers
articles.body:
Brice Turang jumpstarted the offense, Luis Lara delivered the clutch hit and the bullpen was nails, but Garrett Mitchell had another MVP of the Milwaukee Brewers 2-1 Game 1 win over the Los Angeles Dodgers in the National League Championship Series on Oct. 11.

"I think everyone was excited for today," Mitchell said. "Having such amazing fans who support you even when you go down, just keeping the energy up, we feel that and we feed off of that. That's what makes us really good, is it's a collective effort. It's the players on the field, yes, but having that support from the fans is important."

The atmosphere was noticeably livelier than either of the Brewers two home games during their National League Division Series against the San Diego Padres a week ago. Perhaps that's simply due to the advanced stage of the postseason, or maybe there's some extra juice that comes from facing the Dodgers.

But, either way, it was louder from first pitch all the way through the final out, at which point the sellout crowd of 42,617 reached its peak of 114.2 decibels when Mitchell squeezed Mookie Betts' deep fly to center. For much of those NLDS games, the ambient sound sat throughout the action between a floor of 75 decibels and 80 decibels, whereas rarely did it dip beneath 85 dB at any point of when the game was going on in Game 1 against the Dodgers.

Here's how loud it was at different points of the night.

ABS challenge against Shohei Ohtani (3rd inning): 104.5 dB

Jacob Misiorowski exits (5th inning) : 95 dB

Garrett Mitchell leadoff walk (5th inning) : 97.2 dB

Luis Lara's go-ahead single (5th inning) : 106.6 dB

Abner Uribe strikeout of Andy Pages to escape (6th inning): 103.9 dB

Mookie Betts flyout off Aaron Ashby to end inning (7th inning): 95 dB

Freddie Freeman pop-up to open inning (8th inning): 97.1 dB

'Let's Go Brewers' chant between innocuous pitches: 87 dB

Jake Bauers holds base for inning-ending out: 103.1 dB

Trevor Megill enters, stadium speakers blare (9th inning): 103 mph

images.caption: Fans gather at American Family Field for Game 1 of the National League Championship Series between the Milwaukee Brewers and the Los Angeles Dodgers on Oct. 11, 2026 in Milwaukee, Wisconsin. The Brewers beat the Dodgers 2-1.

articles.title: Travis Kelce sends heartfelt message to Cleveland Guardians after booking place in ALCS
articles.summary: Travis Kelce showed love to his hometown Cleveland Guardians after they made it to the American League Championship Series. The Cleveland Guardians pulled of...
articles.body:
Travis Kelce showed love to his hometown Cleveland Guardians after they made it to the American League Championship Series.

The Cleveland Guardians pulled off a spectacular comeback against the Chicago White Sox in the ALDS. After they went down 0-2, they won two games on the road and then booked their berth for the ALCS with a surgical victory in Game 5.

This is the second time in the last three seasons the team has made it this far in the postseason. They lost 4-1 against the New York Yankees in 2024, but they will face the Tampa Bay Rays this time. Naturally, fans are loving this, and that includes a very happy three-time NFL champion.

Travis Kelce tells Cleveland Guardians 'you just have to believe'

Legendary tight end Travis Kelce is a lifelong fan, having been born and raised in Cleveland Heights, Ohio, just six miles away from downtown Cleveland. As a huge fan, he was present at Game 5 of the ALDS when the Guardians secured their berth.

Following the win, the Kansas City Chiefs star was asked about what he thinks of the moment. His reply was electric, and his happiness with the situation was quite evident.

"C'mon, baby! Ay, Cleveland is the reason, baby!" Kelce said. "You just gotta believe, baby. Just gotta believe. ALCS, you know what time it is."

This is shaping up to be a spectacular year for Kelce. Patrick Mahomes is back and the undefeated Chiefs are flying. He got married to Taylor Swift over the summer, too. If the Guardians can somehow make the World Series and win, then it will be more proof that this is Travis' world and everyone else is just living in it.

articles.title: Dodgers shut down by Brewers in NLCS opener as lineup struggles again
articles.summary: MILWAUKEE (AP) — The Los Angeles Dodgers created a handful of scoring opportunities in Game 1 of the NL Championship Series. They ended up with one big hit.
articles.body:
MILWAUKEE (AP) — The Los Angeles Dodgers created a handful of scoring opportunities in Game 1 of the NL Championship Series. They ended up with one big hit.

It's been that kind of October for Los Angeles so far.

The Dodgers went 1 for 6 with runners in scoring position during Sunday night's 2-1 loss to the Milwaukee Brewers. They grounded into three double plays and left nine runners on base.

"Any loss in the playoffs is not great but it's a long series and it's just the first game," first baseman Freddie Freeman said.

The Dodgers have scored a total of 15 runs in their five playoff games so far. They are 2 for 22 with runners in scoring position, adding to the difficulty of their pursuit of a third consecutive World Series championship.

They scored 24 runs and hit .324 with runners in scoring position over their first five postseason games in 2024. They scored 29 times and batted .265 with runners in scoring position over the same period in last year's playoffs.

"We had our chances, but they made plays, pitches when they needed to," Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said after Game 1 against Milwaukee. "We've just got to reset."

Catcher Will Smith is 1 for 19 in the postseason after going 0 for 3 with a walk against the Brewers. Shohei Ohtani is 3 for 16 with no extra-base hits or RBIs. Mookie Betts is 4 for 18.

Betts was the leadoff hitter for the NLCS opener. Smith batted third, and Ohtani was in the cleanup spot. Asked about changing the lineup to help Smith, Roberts acknowledged that was a possibility.

"I think there's always lineup construction," Roberts said. "I can think through — yeah, he's not swinging the bat well. Yeah, we'll see. I just — it's hard because the body of work, and he just has that knack to get a hit, to get a big hit."

Smith batted .276 (16 for 58) with eight RBIs in the postseason last year. He homered twice in the World Series against Toronto.

Los Angeles scored its only run Sunday night when Ohtani scampered home on Andy Pages' single in the second. The Dodgers had the bases loaded when Kiké Hernández bounced into an inning-ending double play against Brewers ace Jacob Misiorowski .

Pages struck out with runners on the corners for the final out of the sixth. Batting with two on and two down in the ninth, Betts flied to the warning track in center.

"That's a great pitching staff," Freeman said. "That's two great pitching staffs. Two great teams going at it. It's kind of what we envisioned."

articles.title: How Brewers squeezed Dodgers to win torturous NLCS opener: 'Gotta love it'
articles.summary: Brewers' victory in NLCS Game 1 proved they won't be pushed around again by Dodgers.
articles.body:
MILWAUKEE — The Milwaukee Brewers knew the magnitude of this one.

It was just Game 1 of the National League Championship Series on Sunday night at American Family Field, but they had their ace, Jacob Misiorowski on the mound. They had a fresh bullpen. They had momentum.

They also had the bitter memory of a year ago that needed to be erased.

You see, the Brewers were in this same position a year ago, facing the mighty Los Angeles Dodgers in the NLCS, with home field advantage.

The Brewers not only were swept, but they didn't lead a single inning, and set a dubious postseason record hitting just .118.

So now, after winning Game 1, 2-1, with their vaunted bullpen picking up Misiorowski and shutting down the Dodgers' powerful offense, just what did this game mean to their psyche?

"Well," said Brewers closer Trevor Megill, "we ain't getting swept now. We can relax a little bit."

Don't let the Brewers fool you. They know how important this game meant for their chances to go where no Brewer team has gone since 1982 with a World Series berth.

"I think that was huge," Brewers left-handed reliever DL Hall said. "Momentum plays a big part in the postseason."

The series wouldn't have been over with a loss, but with World Series MVP Yoshinobu Yamamto taking the mound Monday in Game 2 for the Dodgers, the Brewers simply couldn't afford to head to Los Angeles down 2-0 and still be confident of a return trip to Milwaukee for a potential Game 6.

Now, for the first time since 2021, the Dodgers are trailing in the NLCS, while the Brewers are not only surviving, but embracing their heart-stopping close games.

"You can't go into a long series against a team that has the best record in baseball," Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said, "and expect to just win four. It's going to be a long series. We knew it coming in. We had our chances, but they made plays, pitches when they needed to. We've just got to reset."

The Brewers certainly are developing a knack for these tense moments. They are only the third team in postseason history not to lead or trail by more than two runs in a game, joining the 1915 Red Sox and Phillies. And they are only the fourth club in the last 110 teams to have each of their first five games decided by two or fewer runs.

"Hey," said Brewers center fielder Garrett Mitchell, "it's Brewer baseball. We never give up, man."

It's not as if the Brewers smacked around two-time Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal for five innings or the Dodgers bullpen, producing just six hits the entire game. Their own ace, Misiorowski, lasted just 4 ½ innings. But, oh, that bullpen. It no longer is the best-kept secret in the game.

The Brewers' bullpen, which gave up just two hits in 4 ⅔ shutout innings, has yielded a 0.38 ERA this postseason. They have pitched 23 ⅔ innings in the first five games have a .163 batting average batting average against, with only three extra-base hits, and nine strikeouts.

"Everyone down there throws a sinker," said Aaron Ashby, who pitched two scoreless innings. "Getting the ball on the ground certainly helps limiting damage. And everyone's got a swing-and-miss pitch to offer. So, it helps when you have swing-and-miss stuff in the postseason….

"I just think we have a great combination and variety."

The last time a bullpen had this low of an ERA in the first games of a postseason since the divisional era in 1969 was the 2006 World Series champion St. Louis Cardinals.

"I don't know how you could get more out of them," Brewers manager Pat Murphy said. "We're squeezing everything we can, and they just get better and more confident. They're making pitches and pick each other up.

"They don't care. They just want to get outs for the Milwaukee Brewers, and that's the beauty of it. Everything else that will come their way will be a result of just caring so much about the team and not just about themselves.''

The same attitude is reflected by its offense. They bunted. They hit-and-ran. They moved runners over. They tried to steal. They even got a homer from second baseman Brice Turang.

You get a feeling this could be their year when Turang, who hit just .067 (1-for-15) against the Dodgers in last year's NLCS, hit a 96-mph fastball on the black on the inside part of the plate for a home run to lead off the fourth inning.

"I'm going to tip my hat on a pitch like that," Skubal said. "A 2-0 sinker in, I mean, I'm going to live with that left on left."

Turang, who was working on his swing late into the evening Friday, said it brought back memories growing up and spending the night in the batting cage.

"I just didn't want to foul off my knee again," Turang said. "That's one way to help you stay inside of a ball is hit a ball off your leg or your foot . ... It definitely felt good. It was one of those things where you just are trying to do something, and you end up doing something like that."

It was no different for Brewers 21-year-old rookie Luis Lara, with only 61 games of big-league experience, who stepped up to the plate in the fifth inning. Mitchell led off the inning with a walk. Fellow rookie Cooper Pratt moved him to second with a sacrifice bunt. And Lara slapped a single up the middle on a changeup for a 2-1 lead that the Brewers' bullpen refused to relinquish.

"The dream for me is to win the World Series," he said. "That will be the dream moment is when we're able to complete that. Obviously, very happy that I was able to come through for my teammates and that we were able to get the win."

It's the little things that enabled them to win a major-league leading 103 games this season, despite having the second-lowest home run total in baseball.

"I think the buy-in factor," Turang says, "with everyone buying into what we're trying to accomplish and kind of our style of play. Guys are getting more experience, they're learning the game. That's a big factor in this. Then not giving up when we are behind in the game and knowing that we can do it, we can make up runs.

"This group is really, really good with that.''

They proved that during the season, and now, they're doing it in the postseason, this time for all of the world to see.

"Just Brewers baseball,'' Megill said. "You gotta love it.''
